characters.description: A swordsman and commander of the Moonstream Army whose course remains bound to Emperor Morgan's strategy.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.description: The mother ruling Laskan on behalf of her three-year-old son. She authorizes a covert military escalation, plans to dispose of former orc auxiliaries, and seeks leverage over Morgan while concealing her hand in the operation.
characters.name: Laskan regent

characters.description: An ageless-seeming wizard with mismatched eyes who uses true-word magic to protect a frightened child from nightmares. After restoring the child's calm, he leaves to confront the source of the threat.
characters.name: Ageless wizard

characters.description: An ancient demon serving as an emissary of the Prince of Demons and a longstanding adversary of the ageless wizard. After confronting the wizard over a disrupted nightmare, he is confined for one night in a star-filled prison.
characters.name: Lord of Nightmares

characters.description: An independent warrior recently released from a bargain with the Lord of Nightmares. Despite her earlier conflict with Hadjar, she tries to reach him after the white-haired swordsman's attack and is stopped by an overwhelmingly powerful fire barrier.
characters.name: Desert sabers woman

characters.description: An unidentified swordswoman whose white flame and sword power overwhelm the desert sabers woman. She blocks the attempted rescue and encloses Hadjar with his attacker behind a barrier of fire.
characters.name: White-haired swordswoman

characters.description: An ancient white-haired swordsman who identifies himself as the first disciple in the Darkhan lineage and Hadjar's senior disciple. After driving a blade through Hadjar's heart, he claims that he recovered his mind and now owes Hadjar compensation.
characters.name: Erhard Darkhan

characters.description: Hadjar's close field companion and a senior Moonstream officer. During the crisis around the white-fire barrier, he reasons that its maker may be protecting Hadjar and persuades another warrior to stop a futile assault on it.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: Hadjar's sworn brother and the head of the eighth family. When an imperial rescue order sends Hadjar toward Laskan, Einen is one of the trusted allies Hadjar plans to contact for help before entering hostile territory.
characters.name: Einen

characters.description: The opposing emperor whose schemes concern Laskan's regent as she prepares a covert military escalation and seeks leverage against him.
characters.name: Morgan

characters.description: Morgan's imperial heir, trapped after entering a battle-golem factory in Delphi Valley. Recovering him before the new moon is the stated purpose of the sealed mission that draws Hadjar and his companions into Laskan.
characters.name: Morgan's son

characters.description: A necromancer joining Hadjar's infiltration party at the border. She delivers a spatial ring filled with valuable restorative medicines from an imperial double agent, bringing resources needed for the dangerous mission ahead.
characters.name: Annette

characters.description: Laskan's three-year-old ruler, for whom his mother serves as regent after the death of the previous emperor.
characters.name: Laskan child emperor

characters.description: A free adept hired by the imperial families and reputed to be an exceptional tracker.
characters.name: Masked tracker

characters.description: A gray-haired imperial operative who supplies the rescue party with costly restorative medicines through Annette, then arrives unexpectedly at their border tavern.
characters.name: Secret Office agent

characters.description: An ancient power whose soul fragment is chained inside Hadjar. He offers guidance on the wind's name while plainly stating that he and Hadjar will eventually fight for control of Hadjar's body, making his instruction both valuable and dangerous.
characters.name: The First Darkhan

aliases: Head of a dragon magic pavilion
characters.description: A senior dragon mage who arrives with another official and immobilizes Hadjar's entire party. His intentions and his relationship to the ruling power are not yet clear.
characters.name: Dragon wizard

characters.description: A powerful dragon official responsible for internal and external affairs. After examining Hadjar's blood, he recognizes an unusually strong dragon heritage and a transplanted dragon heart, then orders Hadjar to accompany him.
characters.name: Dragon minister

characters.description: A consciousness-fragment within Hadjar that awakens when the dragon minister insults Hadjar's lineage. It identifies Hadjar as a descendant and begins granting him the White Dragon inheritance.
characters.name: First dragon emperor fragment

characters.description: An ally connected to Einen whom Hadjar plans to contact for help before beginning the rescue mission in Laskan.
characters.name: Dora

characters.description: A powerful Fae messenger who meets Hadjar in an unnatural swamp. She asks him to stop a blood sacrifice on sacred ground, warning that its completion could bring a dark god's shadow into the mortal world.
characters.name: Freya

characters.description: The horned witch oversees captives being killed to empower a seal, with living trees and serpents forming parts of the rite.
characters.name: Horned ritualist

characters.description: The blood rite releases this incomplete manifestation. On encountering Hadjar, it perceives a direct tie between him and a foe from its past, not just ancestry.
characters.name: Dark god's shadow

characters.description: A possibly legendary Laskan swordsman identified as one of the major dangers Hadjar may face while operating inside the empire.
characters.name: Scarlet Swordsman

characters.description: A red-haired Laskan great hero who intervenes when the regent is about to attack an exhausted Hadjar outside the capital.
characters.name: Red-haired Laskan great hero

characters.description: An ancient-seeming Fae warrior who verifies that Hadjar truly knows the wind's name. The knight treats him as a possible future brother in an endless martial cycle and demands a blood oath protecting that knowledge.
characters.name: Winter Court knight

characters.description: The masked tracker in his later-revealed position as leader of the Raven sect. Critically wounded during the abduction, he is carried with Hadjar's party toward Delphi Valley.
characters.name: Raven sect leader

characters.description: Morgan's daughter, whose disappearance before her brother entered Laskan forms part of the imperial rescue assignment given to Hadjar.
characters.name: Imperial princess

characters.description: The imperial empress, whose attempt to use the imperial princess and the Secret Office agent's oath is anticipated by Morgan. Morgan murders her and orders the Secret Office to blame Laskan as a pretext for wider war.
characters.name: Imperial empress

characters.description: Lita's mother and a Fae courtier of the Summer Court. She lives at Little Stream Village with Erhard and Lita, and Hadjar presses her to acknowledge her true nature.
characters.name: Aria

characters.description: Aria's daughter, living with her mother and Erhard at Little Stream Village.
characters.name: Lita

characters.description: The officer who leads scouting work for the Moonstream Army and prepares ambushes during its western-front campaign.
characters.name: Gurum

characters.description: Hadjar's deceased master and a great swordsman once associated with Morgan and the gathered imperial heroes. The war council honors his memory and accepts Hadjar as his disciple, establishing Hadjar's place among them.
characters.name: Orune

characters.description: The head of the imperial Secret Office and one of the powerful figures seated on Morgan's final war council. At this point he appears to be an imperial official participating in the plan to end the war against Laskan.
characters.name: Secret Office chief

characters.description: Laskan's champion in the strongest-warrior duel. Hadjar discovers that he is the earlier red-haired opponent, using a Gemini technique to maintain identities with distinct bodies, auras, and powers.
characters.name: Scarlet Swordsman

characters.description: The dragon assigned to monitor Morgan, previously concealed as the Secret Office chief. He admits the hidden arrangement controlling the human empires and confronts Morgan after the emperor turns the surviving armies against the Dragonlands.
characters.name: Dragonlands monitor

characters.description: The Dragonlands monitor reveals the five-headed true form hidden behind the Secret Office chief. He abandons the pretense of human autonomy and declares that direct control and tribute will replace the concealed arrangement.
characters.name: Five-headed dragon

characters.description: Hadjar's grown tiger companion, who reunites with him after his public death and leaves beside him to seek a path to the Seventh Heaven.
characters.name: Hadjar's tiger companion

recaps.ending: Hadjar kills the Scarlet Swordsman in the strongest-warrior duel, but the fight has stripped both armies of their defenses. The Laskan regent ignites the World River, killing herself, devastating both forces, and causing hundreds of millions of deaths. Tom destroys his own core to save the Moonstream skyship and dies. Morgan then exposes the Dragonlands' hidden rule, kills four concealed dragons, and uses an ancient spear to petrify the five-headed overseer before dying himself. Two years later, Morgan's son is emperor. The Ruby Palace suppresses the truth about the Dragonlands and enforces fifty years of peace among the seven empires. Einen and Dora are raising their son, while Erhard remains with Aria and Lita. Hadjar resigns and arranges his public death, accepting exile from both his empire and former homeland. He deliberately falls back to the Formation Seed stage to gain time for creating his own sword style, then departs with his grown tiger companion in search of the Seventh Heaven. The First Darkhan, the Raven sect, the Fae courts, the Dragonlands, and the dark gods remain unresolved threats.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar survives Erhard Darkhan's forced meditation and gains a deeper bond with the wind. An imperial mission to abduct Laskan's child emperor leads through a dragon confrontation, a dark-god summoning, and the destruction of the Delphi factory, where Morgan's daughter kills the child and dies. Years of war culminate in Hadjar killing the Scarlet Swordsman, only for the Laskan regent's trap to ignite the World River and kill Tom along with hundreds of millions. Morgan exposes the Dragonlands' control, destroys its agents, petrifies their five-headed overseer, and dies. Two years later, Morgan's son rules under a fifty-year peace. Hadjar resigns, fakes his death, reduces his cultivation, and leaves with his tiger companion to seek the Seventh Heaven and build a sword path of his own.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar Darkhan became a formidable swordsman and commander known as the North Wind. He bears a dragon heart, carries an ancient soul fragment connected to the Black General, and remains caught between imperial demands and his own path. Morgan rules Hadjar's empire and can compel his service, while Laskan stands across a long-running war. Hadjar's closest allies include Tom, his field companion, and Einen, his sworn brother. Annette is a necromancer with whom he has worked before. Orune, Hadjar's master, is dead but remains central to his martial inheritance. A desert warrior once tied to the Lord of Nightmares has been released from that bargain. Powerful forces beyond the empires also have claims on Hadjar's future, including the Seventh Heaven, the Fae courts, dragons, demons, and the ancient being bound inside him.

So far this book: Laskan's regent begins a covert escalation against Morgan's empire and plans to eliminate the border orcs once they cease to be useful. Elsewhere, an ancient wizard protects a child from the Lord of Nightmares and delays the demon in a temporary prison. At the border fort, a white-haired swordsman drives a blade through Hadjar's heart while a second white-haired swordswoman seals them behind fire. The attacker is Erhard Darkhan, an ancient emperor and senior disciple in Hadjar's own lineage. He did not intend a simple execution. The wound forces Hadjar into an accelerated meditation, and Erhard binds his survival to Hadjar's while teaching him through memories of the first Darkhan. Hadjar reaches beyond the World River, recognizes a new relationship between his soul and the world, and learns the wind's true name. He awakens able to combine will and energy at a far higher level. After demonstrating this increased strength, Hadjar parts from Erhard, who leaves to protect the mother and child who restored him. Both swordsmen expect their paths to cross again.

The border force grows into the Moonstream Army, but Hadjar has little time to master his new bond with the wind. Morgan's sealed dispatch reports that the crown prince is trapped in a battle-golem factory in Delphi Valley and that the imperial princess vanished before him. Hadjar accepts the rescue mission and travels with Tom to meet Annette. A gray-haired imperial double agent brings a different plan: instead of forcing a way into the factory, they will abduct Laskan's three-year-old emperor and exchange him for Morgan's children. An imperially hired masked tracker joins the operation. His mask is fused to his face, and he has crossed Hadjar's path before. The tracker proposes entering the Laskan capital under merchant cover during the child's birthday, presenting a treasury gift, and using a movement artifact to seize the emperor. Hadjar accepts this as the primary plan while retaining a fallback. The five-person group now has supplies, disguises, and a route into hostile territory, but the palace defenses and the difficulty of identifying and extracting the child remain unresolved.

Hadjar refuses the masked tracker’s renewed invitation to join his ancient mercenary sect, even after the man demonstrates power comparable to Hadjar's. During the journey, Annette recognizes Hadjar's use of the wind's name as a rare form of elemental practice and warns that its traditional users may kill him for possessing it. Seeking guidance, Hadjar enters his soul and consults the First Darkhan. The chained fragment admits that he has been with Hadjar since birth and still expects a future battle for Hadjar's body, but he begins teaching Hadjar about names and the world's origin. The lesson is interrupted when two dragons immobilize the party. A dragon minister examines Hadjar's blood, identifies his dragon heart and heritage, and orders him to submit. An older dragon consciousness within Hadjar answers the insult to his lineage by granting the White Dragon inheritance. Hadjar combines that inheritance with the wind to create Dragon's Dawn, a sword strike powerful enough to wound the minister and split a distant mountain. The effort leaves Hadjar unconscious as the dragon wizard turns against the minister and begins fighting him.

The dragon wizard defeats the minister but is left maimed and near death. Hadjar rescues him, spends valuable medicine to keep him alive, and accepts a reciprocal life-debt. The wizard reveals that he opposes the dragon emperor and hopes to restore justice in his homeland. Hadjar conceals the battle site, shelters the injured dragon, and resumes the Laskan journey while continuing to train with the wind. A supply detour draws the group into a border village where legionaries are abducting local people. Tom kills the immediate captors, and the party raids a nearby camp holding about ten thousand civilians. The captured officer admits that the prisoners are intended for an altar in the woods. Tom frees them, and Hadjar chooses to investigate despite the risk to the imperial mission. He orders his companions to wait for one day and enters an unnatural swamp alone. There he meets Freya, a Fae messenger of the Seventh Heaven. She warns that a blood sacrifice on sacred ground is close to summoning a dark god's shadow into the mortal world and asks Hadjar to stop it.

Hadjar crosses a poisonous Fae swamp and reaches a ritual that is consuming captive souls. He kills the cultivator guarding it and the horned witch conducting it, but the summoning seal has already released a dark god's shadow. Hadjar's strongest attack has no effect, and the entity nearly destroys him before Freya restores his body. The First Darkhan then manifests beside him, recognizes the shadow as an ancient enemy, and briefly takes control of Hadjar's hand and will. Using a recovered lantern, he breaks the seal and forces the shadow away. The confrontation reveals that the dark gods seek the Book of Thousands, intending to rewrite history and turn the four worlds into the void. Hadjar conceals the First Darkhan's intervention from Freya and refuses a reward from the Seventh Heaven because he acted to save civilians. He rejoins his companions at their meeting point. The recovered dragon wizard departs for the Dragonlands, leaving Hadjar a ribbon and the expectation that they will meet again. The infiltration party then reaches the river outside the Laskan capital.

Hadjar's party crosses an ancient bridge into the fortified Laskan capital and enters the imperial birthday festival under merchant cover. The masked tracker and the Secret Office agent carry the prepared gift into the palace while Hadjar, Tom, and Annette wait outside. An explosion destroys the operation's secrecy. The infiltrators emerge wounded, and Tom carries the abducted child emperor. Hadjar uses his movement art to evacuate the group beyond the city but is left exhausted before the regent and six great heroes. A red-haired Laskan champion recognizes him and requests an honorable rematch, refusing to exploit Hadjar's complete depletion. Hadjar restores part of his strength with a pill, and their duel moves above the capital. The two fighters test competing paths through fists, swords, wind, and will. Both are wounded, but neither uses full lethal force near the civilians below. Hadjar finally exploits a disruption in the World River to escape. His companions retain the captive emperor, and the Laskan champion accepts that their next encounter will be fatal.

A Winter Court knight confirms that Hadjar knows the wind's true name and binds him by blood oath never to disclose the name or how he learned it. After three days evading pursuit, Hadjar rejoins his companions, who had believed him dead. They carry the drugged child emperor and the badly wounded masked tracker toward Delphi Valley, but imperial legions block the northern route. The group chooses an abandoned mine beneath the mountains. Before entering, the masked man reveals that he leads the Raven sect and that three soul fragments once resonated through Hadjar and two sect members, awakening the fragment inside Hadjar. He also warns that the sect's leadership is tied to forces shaping Hadjar's life. Annette uses death magic to terrify the mine guards into opening their own defenses, allowing the party to enter and eliminate them. After two days underground, the child emperor protects the sleeping Secret Office agent from a snake, showing courage despite his sheltered upbringing. Hadjar then leads the party out into Delphi Valley, collapses the entrance behind them, and destroys the enemy force waiting below the exit.

Hadjar reaches the battle-golem factory and finds that its commander is Morgan's son. The imperial princess receives the infiltrators, orders treatment for the wounded Raven leader, and remains openly hostile toward the Secret Office agent. She is blind and has lost her cultivation after claiming the Ever-Seeking Spear. Hadjar invokes formal hospitality to protect his party, while the prince makes clear that he expects Hadjar to serve him one day. During the hostage exchange, the princess kills Laskan's child emperor and triggers the destruction of the entire Delphi factory with a concealed imperial power reserve. The blast kills her as well, and the Scarlet Swordsman prevents Hadjar from saving her. Morgan then kills the empress, directs the Secret Office to blame Laskan, and turns the catastrophe into a pretext for wider war. His planning had treated his daughter, the child emperor, and the opposing ruler as pieces in a larger scheme. The hostage mission ends with Morgan's son alive, both royal women dead, Laskan's young ruler dead, and the two empires moving toward decisive conflict.

Morgan sends Hadjar back to train the Moonstream Army for the new war. The deaths at Delphi leave Hadjar questioning his purpose so deeply that his soul and sword begin to fail. He recovers by accepting the opposing emotions bound to his path and creates Peaceful Day, a stance capable of weakening nearby kingdoms. The former Raven leader, having withheld Hadjar from his sect and abandoned its path, is killed by a senior sect swordsman. Einen and Dora's son is born, and Einen asks Hadjar to become the child's godfather through a blood-and-water rite. The family gives Hadjar a renewed reason to fight for a future beyond war. He returns to a Moonstream Army of more than seventy-five thousand soldiers and prepares it to march. Before the campaign, Hadjar visits Little Stream Village and discovers that Erhard is the warrior known there as White Fang. Aria admits that she is a diminished Summer Court Fae. She explains that true names cannot be directly taught and confirms that only four worlds exist, while Erhard continues protecting her and Lita.

Three years of war turn the Moonstream Army into a feared, undefeated force. Ordered to destroy the Whistle Army and burn fields feeding roughly 165 million people, Hadjar refuses to burn the crops. He instead annihilates the opposing force, recording more than eighteen million deaths and becoming increasingly conscious that Morgan has made him an instrument of imperial strategy. The Moonstream Army then joins the enormous final concentration of troops near the Laskan capital. Aboard the empire's great artillery skyship, Morgan convenes his heir, the Secret Office chief, the great heroes, and Hadjar. The council recognizes Hadjar as effectively equal to a great hero and honors Orune as his deceased master. Morgan announces that the war will end in three days. The Laskan regent has invoked an ancient strongest-warrior duel whose oaths will leave both armies vulnerable to her larger plan. Morgan identifies Hadjar as his empire's strongest warrior and the only one capable of facing the Scarlet Swordsman. Hadjar accepts the duel, believing Morgan has also offered an important promise that remains unstated.

Hadjar enters the strongest-warrior duel and discovers that the Scarlet Swordsman is the same earlier opponent who fought him under another identity, using Gemini to maintain distinct bodies and powers. The Laskan champion once spared Hadjar because of a debt to Orune, but now fights to preserve his own legend. He is faster, stronger, and far richer in energy. Hadjar refuses artifacts and disables his neural network rather than surrender control of the contest. By invoking a true word through the memory of those who shaped him, Hadjar finally wounds his opponent. The Scarlet Swordsman's last technique carries the history of a village destroyed after bandits stole its harvest, a tragedy in which Orune was involved. Hadjar answers with Peaceful Day, pierces an armor joint, and lets his sword consume the champion's energy body until he dies. Hadjar survives almost powerless. The duel has also exhausted the defenses of both massed armies, exactly as the Laskan regent intended. The World River ignites around them, beginning the larger attack hidden behind the formal contest.

The burning World River devastates both armies and kills hundreds of millions. Tom destroys his own core to save the Moonstream skyship and dies, leaving his armor and bottle. Morgan reveals that the Laskan regent sacrificed herself and her son to power the attack. With the old imperial war effectively ended, he calls on survivors from both sides to unite against the Ruby Palace and Dragonlands, exposing the fiction of human independence. Four hidden dragons confirm that the empires have been manipulated and taxed by higher rulers. Morgan destroys them with true words, suffering mortal damage. The Secret Office chief then admits that he is the dragon assigned to monitor Morgan and reveals a five-headed true form. He declares that hidden control will now become open domination. Morgan answers with an ancient spear deceived by blood magic into recognizing him as his son. The weapon petrifies the dragon atop the newly formed Dragon Ridge. Morgan dies after completing the strike, with a final vision of reunion with Orune and his family. His rebellion succeeds in exposing the truth, but its consequences pass to the survivors.

Two years after the battle at Dragon Ridge, Morgan's son has become emperor. The Ruby Palace suppresses every public reference to the Dragonlands and imposes a fifty-year ban on war among the seven empires. Hadjar visits Einen and Dora's family before ending his old life. He resigns as general and arranges for the world to believe that he died of his wounds, accepting that he can no longer return openly to his empire or former homeland. Einen and Hadjar reaffirm their brotherhood before parting. Hadjar then deliberately cripples his cultivation back to the Formation Seed stage. The sacrifice gives him about 125 years in which to create a sword style that is truly his own rather than remain confined by inherited paths and command obligations. Reunited with his now-grown tiger companion, he leaves to continue searching for a route to the Seventh Heaven. Tom and Morgan are dead, Morgan's heir rules, and the old war is over. The First Darkhan, the Raven sect, the Fae powers, the Dragonlands, and the dark gods remain unresolved.

characters.description: Sedent's reclusive sword master, still alive after the wider world came to believe him dead. He defeats a formidable visiting swordsman with a cherry twig, then accepts Gustaf into a school open to anyone willing to learn.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.description: A veteran wandering swordsman who challenges schools and collects their signs while seeking the threshold of true cultivation. His journey to Sedent brings him to the local master's unusually inclusive school.
characters.name: Gustaf

characters.description: A Sedent blacksmith who respects the town's grey-haired sword master. He directs Gustaf to the master's school while warning that the proposed challenge is unlikely to end well.
characters.name: Jarg

characters.description: A powerful swordsman who repeatedly challenges Sedent's unnamed master, using two swords and wagering wine and stories on their latest bout.
characters.name: Dual-sword visitor

characters.description: A small white feline with black stripes who remains beside Sedent's unnamed sword master.
characters.name: Sedent master's feline companion

characters.description: A gravely wounded half-demon woman whom Hadjar met decades earlier. She reaches his school and asks him for help.
characters.name: Demon hunter

characters.description: The small feline beside Sedent's master is Hadjar's long-term tiger companion. She dislikes the wounded hunter but obeys Hadjar's order to guard her.
characters.name: Hadjar's tiger companion

characters.description: Hadjar's deceased master, whose inherited technique now limits Hadjar's remaining life. Hadjar must create a personal sword style capable of overcoming that restriction before his aging body fails.
characters.name: Orune

characters.description: A white-haired swordsman of exceptional power who organizes a seven-empire force for war with the Ruby Palace and calls Hadjar to take part.
characters.name: White-haired army leader

characters.description: A long-serving true cultivator responsible for Sedent's welfare. He tolerates the wounded hunter's presence but presses Hadjar to investigate the blight associated with the Nightmare Trench.
characters.name: Sedent's governor

characters.description: The demon ruler of a hidden city reached through the Nightmare Trench. He commands exceptionally strong armored guards from a fortified castle while human captives live under the city's control.
characters.name: Demon City lord

characters.description: An ancient presence within Hadjar who calls him a disciple. Through a memory of his former service to Durger, he directs Hadjar toward the Demon City lord as a possible source of knowledge about the Pool of Many Reflections.
characters.name: The First Darkhan

characters.description: A god of war once served by the First Darkhan. In an ancient memory, he petrifies the Potter's beloved, whose tears sustain a pool through which the gods can observe mortals.
characters.name: Durger

characters.description: A Heaven Emperor swordsman serving within the Demon City lord's castle. He detects the advanced sword skill hidden beneath Hadjar's alchemist disguise but allows the audience to proceed and proposes a future duel.
characters.name: Demon City valet

characters.description: An ancient human wizard encountered in the First Darkhan's memory. At the grave of a woman he loved, Ash warns the First Darkhan to restrain his destructive power and acknowledges that his own war against the Seventh Heaven disturbed the boundaries of the four worlds.
characters.name: Ash

characters.description: An elderly hunter who detects danger approaching a borderland village camp. He arms himself and places a young villager behind him for protection.
characters.name: Elder hunter

characters.description: An ancient and extremely powerful agent of the demon prince who visits Hadjar during his village recovery. He recognizes that Hadjar deliberately broke his own meridians and warns that destroying the demon outpost has made him a target.
characters.name: Demon prince's emissary

characters.description: The man known as White Fang. He approaches Hadjar's new home intending to force him into a coming war, with death as the alternative if Hadjar refuses.
characters.name: Erhard Darkhan

characters.description: Hadjar's former demon-hunter companion, now his wife. They exchange wedding bracelets and establish a committed household in the village where she works as a healer.
characters.name: Hadjar's wife

characters.description: A supernatural emissary who identifies the ice prison holding Hadjar's family as Icy Sorrow. He says he represents one of four powers that guide the world and is generally barred from interfering directly with mortals.
characters.name: Lord of Nightmares

characters.description: The woman who claims responsibility for imprisoning Hadjar's wife and unborn child. From the Seventh Heaven, where she has gone to serve the god of war, she demands that Hadjar reach her before she will release them.
characters.name: Hadjar's estranged daughter

characters.description: The spirit guardian of the fire flower in the Dark Woods. It refuses Hadjar's request, says he cannot repair the forest's accumulated wounds, and consumes the flower rather than let him take it.
characters.name: Dark Woods keeper

aliases: sister of the Winter Court queen
characters.description: A fey ruler hostile to Hadjar because of his alignment with her sister's Winter Court. She halts his attempt to finish the Dark Woods keeper and tells him how long the captives in Icy Sorrow have left.
characters.name: Summer Court queen

characters.description: A dragon mage and old acquaintance of Hadjar. He arrives as Hadjar defeats a pavilion mentor, prevents the confrontation from becoming fatal, and grants Hadjar the audience he demanded.
characters.name: Magic Dawn Pavilion sage

characters.description: The ruler of the Dragonlands and controller of the Ruby Palace treasury. Hadjar agrees to assist the pavilion sage in overthrowing him so that the treasury can be reached.
characters.name: Dragon Emperor

characters.description: The imperial princess scheduled to join a delegation to the Ruby Mountains. Hadjar must win the Hero Challenge and return her safely to earn the Emperor's oath granting him one wish.
characters.name: Dragon Emperor's daughter

characters.description: A formidable warrior discussed among the likely Hero Challenge contenders. Despite her recognized ability, Dragonlands tradition is expected to bar her from entering because she is a woman.
characters.name: Excluded female warrior

characters.description: The ice-wielding finalist whose armor concealed the woman barred from the Hero Challenge by tradition. Hadjar's attack exposes her identity during their final duel, and officials remove her from the contest for entering in disguise.
characters.name: Armored female finalist

recaps.ending:
Hadjar's wife and their unborn son Nero remain alive but soul-bound inside Icy Sorrow. The Lord of Nightmares hides the prison in an ice palace, and the fire flower is unavailable after the Summer Court queen orders the Dark Woods keeper to consume it. Hadjar therefore accepts a six-century deadline to reach the Seventh Heaven, confront his estranged daughter, and rescue his family. He pursues godhood through the Path Through the Stars.

The Magic Dawn Pavilion sage joins Hadjar in a plot against the Dragon Emperor. Hadjar wins the Hero Challenge when his armored opponent is exposed as the woman barred by tradition, then takes a life-binding oath to escort the imperial princess to the Ruby Mountains and return her safely. Success should earn a wish that can open the Emperor's treasury, although the Emperor recognizes Hadjar and is deliberately allowing the scheme to advance. Erhard remains at war with the Dragonlands, Hadjar's tiger companion has left and may be drawn into Durger's service, and the demon prince's response to the destroyed Demon City gate remains unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar lives in concealment as Sedent's aging sword master, racing to create a personal style before Orune's legacy kills him. A wounded demon hunter draws him into the hidden Demon City, where they incite an uprising and stop its lord from opening a gate to the mortal world. Hadjar founds the Music of the Wind Sword, destroys the gate, and later marries the hunter in a remote village. His attempt at peace ends when their unborn son Nero and his mother are sealed in Icy Sorrow by Hadjar's estranged daughter. With six centuries to reach the Seventh Heaven or find another cure, Hadjar seeks the Path Through the Stars. He allies with the Magic Dawn Pavilion sage against the Dragon Emperor, wins the Hero Challenge after an excluded woman is exposed in the final, and swears to return the Emperor's daughter safely from the Ruby Mountains. The oath opens a possible route to the imperial treasury, but the Emperor already knows Hadjar's purpose and intends to use him.

recaps.text:
Previously: Hadjar Darkhan survived decades of warfare, cultivation, and conflict with powers far beyond the mortal world. He carries an ancient soul fragment associated with the First Darkhan and was trained by Orune, whose legacy continues to shape his path. The wider world regards Hadjar as a legendary swordsman, but his victories have left him questioning the cost of endless advancement and bloodshed.

Hadjar's closest bonds include a powerful white tigress who has accompanied him for years and figures from earlier struggles whose ambitions still reach across kingdoms. Morgan is dead. The gods and the Seventh Heaven also remain entangled with Hadjar's fate. At the opening of this volume, Hadjar has withdrawn from public life rather than resolved those larger conflicts.

So far this book: Gustaf, a wandering swordsman, arrives in Sedent hoping to challenge its reclusive master. The master proves to be Hadjar Darkhan, alive despite his supposed death and living as an aged, scarred teacher. Hadjar defeats a powerful old friend with a cherry twig and accepts Gustaf as a disciple without imposing special terms. His school welcomes anyone, and teaching others has become part of his attempt to discover a sword style that is truly his own.

Hadjar's visiting friend is also a senior general. He reports that cultivators from all seven empires are gathering south of Sakashim under a white-haired leader who plans a united war against the Ruby Palace. Hadjar recognizes that the campaign may serve ambitions beyond its declared enemy and could unleash further wars after victory. He refuses the summons, choosing his secluded school and unfinished personal path over another vast conflict. The general leaves angry, while Hadjar remains in Sedent with his disciples and deceptively small white feline companion.

Hadjar's simulations show that ordinary training cannot save him: he has only a little more than fifty years to create a personal style and undo the deadly limit imposed by Orune's technique. Before he can solve that problem, a grievously wounded half-demon hunter reaches his school with demonic pursuers behind her. Hadjar and his tiger companion stabilize her damaged energy body, and Hadjar destroys the attacking vanguard.

Sedent's governor explains that the hunter was hired to investigate the Nightmare Trench, which is blamed for a spreading regional blight. He pressures Hadjar to assist if the school is to remain welcome in the city. Hadjar and the hunter test one another in a duel, confirming that his aged body still conceals extraordinary control even though he has not drawn his true sword for decades. The hunter then reveals what lies below the trench: a separate Demon City where humans are enslaved, armored guards protect a fortified castle, and a demon ruler holds power. She survived almost six months in hiding there before escaping. Hadjar now faces a hidden realm rather than a simple local disturbance.

Hadjar, the demon hunter, and the white tigress travel to the Nightmare Trench. Hadjar plans to use the hunter's blood to pass as her demon husband, but the crossing first subjects him to visions. The First Darkhan shows him an ancient memory of serving Durger and directs him toward the Demon City lord for knowledge about the Pool of Many Reflections.

Inside the artificial world beyond the trench, Hadjar learns that the lord is a Heaven Emperor preparing the Trial of the Heavens and Earth in pursuit of immortality. The hunter favors killing him during the trial, while Hadjar develops a broader plan. Disguised as a married demon couple, they gather complaints about taxation, merchants, and slave prices. Hadjar enters the city as an alchemist, surveys its streets as they rearrange every twelve hours, and notices that its sewers and waterworks remain fixed. He then contaminates the water with dust from his blue blade and opens a free clinic that secretly provides the cure. The resulting epidemic makes residents depend on his healer identity and prompts the afflicted city lord to summon him into the castle.

A Heaven Emperor valet detects Hadjar's concealed sword mastery but permits his alchemist disguise to stand. Hadjar treats the Demon City lord and learns that the ruler will soon attempt his heavenly trial during a bloody eclipse. As payment, Hadjar receives information about the Pool of Many Reflections. The lord also boasts of an earlier crossing into the human world and admits killing the golden-haired mother of Hadjar's brother, giving Hadjar a personal reason to end him.

Hadjar and the hunter move from manufactured illness to manufactured scarcity. They decide to exploit the city's fragile food supply, and Hadjar burns four upper-district warehouses while leaving the poor district's stores intact. An axe-wielding demon tracks him through the disguise. Hadjar wins, but the exertion badly strains his aging body, and the attacker destroys his own energy center rather than reveal more. The hunter admits the dead demon was her uncle and that she concealed the true purpose of her mission. Her missing sister may be imprisoned in the city, which is being prepared as an outpost for a future Demon Parade. Hadjar and the hunter finally commit as partners to find the sister, kill the lord, and destroy the city.

The hunter explains that the Demon Parade has accelerated from a distant threat to one expected in roughly six centuries because the boundaries of four worlds were damaged about a century ago. Her demon father and his brother were sent to establish mortal-world positions, and her bloodline led her to this city. The First Darkhan warns that the city lord is building an actual gate to the demon world.

Food prices rise, unrest spreads, and a riverside quarry offers a possible route to the construction project. Hadjar and the hunter intercept the final seasonal food caravan, facing disciplined guards rather than ordinary refugee defenders. Hadjar's wind-and-sword images break their formation, and Dragon Storm destroys the remaining resistance, but every major technique worsens his condition. During the aftermath, Hadjar witnesses another memory. Ash, an ancient wizard, acknowledges that his failed war against the Seventh Heaven disrupted the four-world boundary. The First Darkhan interprets the coming crisis as another recurring Demon Parade and declares that Hadjar will eventually have to fight Ash, an opponent even the First Darkhan could not defeat.

The caravan battle leaves Hadjar unconscious for four days, nearly blind, and with only a few years of life remaining. He nevertheless stays in the Demon City. After helping starving residents, he provokes the lord's valet and accepts arrest on a false debt charge so he can be sent to the quarries. His seizure becomes the spark for open revolt, and he deliberately frames the guards for a child's death to ensure the uprising spreads.

At the quarry, Hadjar learns that the hunter's missing sister died in a rockslide. The rebels time their attack to the city lord's heavenly trial, and the hunter brings Hadjar to the gate. She holds off the valet while Hadjar attacks the lord, but his weakened strike fails. As he falls, Hadjar finally understands his personal path as music expressed through his blade. His youth, sight, cultivation, and sword return, and he names the new path the Music of the Wind Sword. Hadjar severs the finger bearing the lord's protective ring. The next heavenly sword kills the lord and destroys the gate, the palace foundation, and much of the city. Hadjar and the hunter escape to the mortal world, where his tigress confronts them.

Hadjar's white tigress reveals that Orune trained her and left her a sword. Jealous of the demon hunter, she challenges Hadjar, but he refuses to fight and lets her blade pierce him. He tells her that he loves her as a daughter and that she must choose her own path. She departs, leaving Hadjar wounded beside the hunter.

The pair reach a remote border village after Hadjar kills a dire bear that attacked its hunters. The demon hunter treats the wounded, and the village chief gives them shelter for winter. Hadjar's damaged meridian prevents proper combat for months, so he works fields and learns carpentry while his companion becomes the village healer. An ancient emissary of the demon prince confirms that Hadjar broke his own meridians deliberately. He warns that the destroyed outpost may lead the prince to open uncontrolled portals and that Hadjar's peaceful refuge will endanger those around him. Hadjar rejects the warning and chooses domestic life. At the harvest gathering, he and the hunter exchange wedding bracelets. As they establish themselves as husband and wife, Erhard, now called White Fang, approaches with an ultimatum to join his war or die.

Erhard reaches Hadjar's home as a Heaven Emperor and ancient last king. He argues that the fractured world must be remade through war and identifies the Dragonlands as an enemy. Hadjar refuses, explaining that years of manipulation and killing have destroyed his faith in advancement at any cost. His tiger companion sides with Erhard's belief that strength alone preserves choice. When Hadjar insists on a mortal future of family and service, she declares that the warrior she loved is gone and leaves him.

Erhard then forces Hadjar into a sequence of memories. As conqueror of the Hundred Kingdoms, Erhard ruled through terror before attempting to stop expanding. A dragon ambassador later demanded another campaign to secure land for a growing dragon population. Erhard chose peace and his pregnant wife instead, hoping eventually to pass on the crown and retire. The refusal enabled a conspiracy: the ambassador exploited a loophole in the ruler's oath, rebel knights murdered Erhard's wife, and a dagger placed Erhard in a deathlike magical sleep. Erhard presents this betrayal as proof that a powerful leader cannot abandon war without exposing loved ones to the consequences.

Erhard spares Hadjar and his wife but predicts they will meet on a future battlefield. After the tiger companion's departure, a novice of Durger approaches her. Hadjar remains in the village, embraces restraint, and builds an ordinary life through hunting, repairs, and aid to poorer neighbors. Nearly eight months pass as he and his wife plan a larger home and family.

A bandit group tries to extort Hadjar and threatens his wife. He defeats their leader without killing him and leaves to report the men to the guards. Before he goes, his wife reveals that she is pregnant with their son. Hadjar chooses the name Nero Darkhan and resolves to give the child an honorable life unlike his own. His hope lasts only until he senses danger and races home. The house has been wrecked, and his wife is sealed inside an ice sarcophagus. Hadjar can still sense both her soul and Nero's, proving that they remain alive, but an unseen speaker stops him from striking the prison.

The Lord of Nightmares identifies the prison as Icy Sorrow, a flower from Durger's garden that binds life, energy, will, and soul. Breaking it would shatter the captives' souls. A letter reveals that Hadjar's estranged daughter imprisoned his family and went to the Seventh Heaven to serve the god of war, demanding that Hadjar reach her. The Lord of Nightmares says the scheme may be intended to turn Hadjar into a weapon against the Jasper Emperor, but offers a possible cure: the opposing fire flower.

Hadjar travels to the spirit world's Dark Woods, where the keeper refuses his request and consumes the fire flower. Hadjar fights the Shi in its own domain and decapitates it, but the forest sustains the keeper. The Summer Court queen then prevents Hadjar from using the Lord of Nightmares' fire-staff splinter. She admits ordering the keeper to withhold the flower and says Icy Sorrow will kill Hadjar's wife and child in six centuries. The Lord of Nightmares hides the prison in a protected ice palace. Unable to obtain the flower, Hadjar abandons peace, vows to reach the Seventh Heaven, and sets out for the Path Through the Stars as a route toward godhood.

Hadjar climbs the 7,777 steps to the Magic Dawn Pavilion and demands an audience with its sage. A mentor tries to stop him with dragon true-word magic, but Hadjar analyzes the unfamiliar spells and places his sword at the mentor's throat. The sage, an old acquaintance, intervenes and agrees to work with Hadjar against the Dragon Emperor. Hadjar needs access to the imperial treasury, while the sage seeks revenge for the Emperor's murder of his daughter and grandson.

Their plan uses the coming Ruby and Dragon festival. Hadjar must win the Hero Challenge, protect the Emperor's daughter during a delegation to the Ruby Mountains, and return her safely. The Emperor's oath would then grant Hadjar one wish, allowing him to request entry to the treasury and seek the Path Through the Stars. In the Ruby Palace, Hadjar sees the Dragonlands' extraordinary wealth and military strength and learns that his scarlet sword is a divine predatory weapon that grows by consuming spirits. He enters the contest as a commoner. The Dragon Emperor, however, already recognizes Hadjar, knows the treasury is his objective, suspects the pavilion sage's plot, and deliberately chooses to let Hadjar proceed because he intends to use him first.

The Dragon Emperor's daughter opens the Hero Challenge, and ninety-six candidates enter its initial free-for-all. Safety amulets immediately remove eight of them, leaving eighty-eight contestants to continue without artifacts. Hadjar avoids the opening fighting by moving unseen through the wind. An armored contestant then uses a powerful ice technique to eliminate nearly everyone else, forcing Hadjar to answer with his wind-and-dragon sword style. He breaks the ice assault and reaches the final as the only remaining opponent.

The armored finalist wields a divine ice sword and a heavy-sword technique that nearly overwhelms Hadjar. His Dragon's Dawn attack exposes her as the formidable woman excluded from the contest by tradition. Officials remove her for entering in disguise, leaving Hadjar the winner. He becomes the imperial princess's appointed protector and swears a life-binding oath under ancient law to return her safely from the Ruby Mountains. The victory advances his plan to earn access to the treasury and obtain the Path Through the Stars, but it also binds his life to a mission that has not begun. His wife and unborn Nero remain imprisoned in Icy Sorrow, the six-century rescue deadline continues, and the Dragon Emperor knowingly waits behind the arrangement.

recaps.ending: Hadjar gives the imprisoned First Warrior the battle-death that ends Durger's punishment and releases Tened and Itia unharmed. Outside the prison, the apparent rescue becomes a betrayal. Tash'Magan is exposed as an organizer of the assassination scheme, and Tened admits her own part by stabbing Hadjar with a poisoned dagger. Tash pushes him from the cliff, but Hadjar's white tigress catches him and carries him away. Abraham Shensie's group later finds Hadjar alive but critically poisoned, while Tened and Tash escape. Sin'Magan, Shi'ak Min, and Tash's wounded sister have no confirmed final condition. Hadjar's wife and unborn child remain imprisoned in Icy Sorrow. His six-century lifespan limit, the identity-threatening First Darkhan inheritance, the demon-prince bargain, the Dragon Emperor's designs, and the wider conflict involving Ash, Helmer, and Durger all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar joins an imperial delegation to protect Princess Tened on the road to the Ruby Mountains while seeking a route to rescue his imprisoned family. After surviving the Red Mist and stopping the Raven Sect from taking the First Darkhan's North Wind Country inheritance, he returns burdened by a six-century lifespan limit. A Highlander coup destroys the delegation, forcing Hadjar and Tened into Abraham Shensie's caravan and through the Port of the Dead. In a dead god's prison, Hadjar borrows the First Darkhan's law without surrendering his identity and grants the First Warrior a freeing death. The rescued Tened then reveals her complicity in the assassination plot: she poisons Hadjar, and Tash'Magan throws him from a cliff. Hadjar's white tigress saves him from the fall, but Abraham's group finds him critically poisoned as Tened and Tash escape.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar Darkhan, a human-dragon swordsman, is pursuing a path toward the Seventh Heaven while trying to free his wife and unborn child from imprisonment in Icy Sorrow. A fragment and inheritance of the First Darkhan reside within him, creating both a source of power and an unresolved danger. Hadjar also has an absent supernatural white tigress companion.

Hadjar is assigned to protect Princess Tened during a two-year imperial journey to the Ruby Mountains. Chin'Ameh confirms that the Dragon Emperor knows Hadjar's identity and warns him to find an unexpected solution now that the planned treasury route is blocked. Sin'Magan commands the guard detail, while Tash'Magan and her sister serve as Tened's personal bodyguards and Shi'ak Min leads the mages. The princess gives Hadjar an imperial-blood wreath needed to cross the Red Mist Lands. The artifact protects Tened from non-immortal attacks, but it can also compel Hadjar and prevent him from revealing the journey's secrets. In the spirit world, the ruler of the Red Mist forces Hadjar to battle a puppet made from Dogar's dead echo. Hadjar restores a moment of Dogar's awareness and honors his commander's sacrifice. The trial ends, although Tened must use the wreath to stop Hadjar from attacking the Red Mist. After Hadjar and Tened leave through the portal, Freya punishes the Red Mist for disturbing an honored dead warrior.

With the Red Mist behind them, Hadjar remains troubled by the wreath's coercive power. Tash enforces their promised first-blood duel under rules that allow only swordsmanship. Her Ice-Breath Sword Style exploits the gaps in Hadjar's new Blue Wind Sword Song Style, and she wins. The delegation then finds a burned village whose victims had their energy structures removed. Hadjar connects the atrocity to the Raven Sect, and Shi'ak Min detects more than two thousand sect members ahead. A detour would add years to the journey, endangering Hadjar's captive wife and unborn child. Hadjar proposes reconnaissance, and Tash joins him both to watch him and to avenge relatives killed by the sect. Under a temporary concealment cloak, they discover prisoners being sacrificed to feed an ancient altar. Reinforcements cannot arrive before the ritual finishes, so the two scouts prepare an immediate attempt to destroy it. Sin'Magan's emergency ring may be their only means of stopping the ritual.

The First Darkhan tells Hadjar that the Raven Sect is opening a passage to the North Wind Country, the refuge he founded after rebelling against the Jasper Emperor. The sect wants an inheritance like the one already placed within Hadjar. Hadjar and Tash infiltrate the camp, but the concealment fails to hide the soul fragment inside him and both are captured. Tash is badly wounded. While bound, she reveals that the Dragon Emperor knows Hadjar is a half-breed and intends to steal the Path Through the Stars scroll. She accepts the truth and helps him escape. Hadjar disables her to keep her from fighting while injured, reaches the altar, and learns that the sect is using the First Darkhan's belt as its gate. He activates Sin'Magan's ring and throws it into the ritual. The explosion ruins the camp and disrupts the ceremony, but a vortex pulls Hadjar and the sect members into the belt. Tash awakens outside with the belt intact and no ability to sense Hadjar through the World River.

Hadjar awakens in the North Wind Country with only days to return to Tened. After the Raven Sect members die fighting a spirit-level guardian, he kills the wounded creature and is rescued by an ancient Fae who is his distant maternal ancestor. She explains that his dragon heart awakened several bloodlines and warns that the sect has reached the temple holding the First Darkhan's inheritance. Hadjar crosses the remnants of a peaceful multiracial city and a necropolis filled with exiled immortals. He refuses every offered inheritance, including one that claims it could free his family, because accepting would endanger both him and the refuge. At the final chamber he finds the Raven Sect leader dead, unable to pay the required price. With the First Darkhan's consent, Hadjar kills the ancient rebel's preserved beloved and destroys the belt that provided access. He returns to Tash outside the ruined ritual site. The North Wind Country is protected from immediate capture, but Hadjar has accepted a lifespan limited to six hundred years while the inheritance matures within him.

Nearly a month after Hadjar's return, the delegation finds a dragon soldier murdered by a precise feather-shaped wound. The locked chamber and access to the protected camp suggest an internal killer. Flaming feather-arrows then strike Tened's meeting room. Shi'ak Min shields the group until the attack overwhelms him, while Tash's sister suffers devastating wounds. Shi'ak Min encases her in stone to preserve her temporarily, and Tash spends much of her strength clearing an escape route. The assault proves to be a coordinated coup involving close to a thousand traitors within the delegation. At the waterfall route, the former accountant reveals Heaven Emperor-level power and shoots Shi'ak Min. With Tened unconscious and the rest of the defenders trapped or injured, Hadjar escapes along the path through the clouds. He and the princess are now separated from Sin'Magan, Tash'Magan, Tash's sister, and Shi'ak Min, whose outcomes are unknown.

Hadjar discovers poison among Tened's medicines, confirming that the conspiracy reached the delegation's supplies. Tened shares the secret route map, but they conclude that both the official road and direct contact with the Dragon Emperor could serve the attackers' political aims. Hadjar disguises Tened as the human cartographer Gevena Usense and takes her into a trading town to find a merchant caravan. Two pursuers follow them. Abraham Shensie, a weapons dealer traveling toward the Ruby Mountains, offers passage after testing Hadjar with a thrown dagger. The pursuers identify themselves as Highlanders seeking restored dragon rule and admit that they have sacrificed lifespan for Phoenix power. Hadjar draws them outside and kills both. Tened asks him to use her personal name as their reliance on each other deepens. Abraham then exposes flaws in their cartographer story, but still permits them to join his group on the condition that neither side asks about the other's hidden business. Hadjar accepts despite recognizing that the arrangement contains an undisclosed risk.

Abraham introduces Itia and Gustaf, former soldiers armed with a whip and bow, and explains that Guy will join them later. The crew plans to evade dwarf patrols through an abandoned mine reached by an old port. Each former soldier knows only part of the route, while they need Hadjar's sword against the undead. Helmer, the Lord of Nightmares, visits Hadjar on behalf of a demon prince and proposes a blood bargain. Hadjar secures a future favor from the prince before learning the price: he must kill an immortal inside the maze. Helmer admits that he previously protected Hadjar from the prince's retaliation but cannot help with the killing. The group meets Guy at the ancient ruins, and Hadjar's repeated mental simulations offer no plausible victory over an immortal swordsman. At dawn, the party enters the Port of the Dead. Its paths contain soul-damaging feathers, deceptive familiar faces, and ancient undead. With no safe retreat and only limited local rules to guide them, they cross deeper toward the supposed mine passage.

Inside the Port of the Dead, Abraham's group learns that the tainted undead are far stronger than expected and can be ended only by destroying the green death-flame in their chests. Guy's predatory axe and Hadjar's scarlet sword can accomplish this, but concentrated power attracts more enemies. The group shelters in a temple protected by the fading will of Aksor. Freya privately warns Hadjar not to seek the maze's immortal and offers to have the gods cancel his demon-prince bargain if he stays away. When Aksor's protection fails, a vast undead host led by an armored skeletal rider surrounds the temple. The First Darkhan's fragment recognizes the rider as the First Warrior. Hadjar cuts a path through the horde, badly damaging his body because his spirit and techniques have outgrown it. Tened summons a Star Forest of starlight trees that restrains much of the host, but the spell exhausts her and reveals her dragon features. Hadjar carries her onward while the restraint fails and the party remains half a mile from the underground entrance.

The party fights toward the well that leads underground, with Gustaf's arrows and Itia's whip helping clear the route. Hadjar makes Abraham swear to take Tened into the well, then challenges the First Warrior alone. He destroys the rider's undead horse and survives a duel against overwhelming physical force, but cannot break the warrior's armor or chest-flame. Abraham pulls the badly wounded Hadjar into the well before the killing blow. Underground, the group discovers that Abraham's smuggling story was false. His father, Joppa Shensie, recovered part of a map to a dead god's tomb, and Abraham's crew is following its marked route through a maze. The rumored prize is a technique capable of raising a seeker to the dead god's level. The map remains incomplete, and the maze contains mental traps and monsters. Hadjar suspects that this dead god is connected to the immortal named in his bargain. Despite the deception and the danger, the entire party enters the maze.

The maze turns nightmares into threats when travelers answer them with too much power. It traps Hadjar in visions of his former world, lost relationships, and personal failures, while another creature seizes Gustaf in a convulsive illusion. During the confusion, Tened and Itia are pulled into the moving darkness above the maze. Hadjar follows to rescue them, telling Abraham's remaining group to continue after three days if he does not return. More visions accuse Hadjar through the images of his parents, brother, former companions, and white tigress, but he refuses to let guilt define him. He reaches the imprisoned dead god, who mistakes him for the First Darkhan because of the soul fragment he carries. The captive identifies himself as the First Darkhan's former subordinate, comrade, and enemy, and holds Tened and Itia. Before Hadjar can resolve the confrontation, the First Darkhan draws him into an inner world and begins showing him the history that links the prisoner to the mortal lands.

The First Darkhan's memories reveal that the First Warrior once came to challenge him after accepting Durger's accusation that he had abandoned divine service. Instead of fighting immediately, the First Darkhan made the warrior experience ordinary village life. Over three years, the warrior weakened his soul body, came to value mortal labor and existence, and argued that mortals deserved cultivation rather than contempt. When Durger attacked, he drew the assault over the ocean and sacrificed himself to save the village and its people. Durger punished that choice by imprisoning him eternally as a dead god. The First Darkhan asks Hadjar to grant the warrior a true battle-death and lends him the necessary power. Hadjar returns to the prison knowing that complete acceptance of either inheritance would erase his own identity. Mortal techniques cannot harm a god, so he finds the First Darkhan's black-sword law and opposes the warrior's axe law. When an inner voice urges him to abandon his humanity, Boreas intervenes. Hadjar rejects assimilation and returns to the duel with the black sword in the First Warrior's chest.

The First Warrior accepts Hadjar's strike as the freedom he sought and dies, ending Durger's imprisonment. Tened and Itia are released unharmed, and Hadjar realizes that the prisoner used them to compel the freeing duel rather than to kill them. Outside the prison at Ruby Mountain, Hadjar identifies Tash'Magan as an organizer of the assassination scheme. Tened then reveals that she is also part of the plot. She stabs Hadjar with a poisoned dagger, and Tash pushes him from the cliff. Hadjar's white tigress returns in human guise, catches his falling body, and removes him from immediate danger. Abraham Shensie's group later finds Hadjar alive but critically poisoned. Tened and Tash escape. The condition of the companions left during the coup remains unconfirmed, while Hadjar's captive family, limited lifespan, demon-prince bargain, conflict with the Dragon Emperor, and dangerous First Darkhan inheritance all remain unresolved.

characters.name: Hadjar

characters.name: Nero

characters.name: Serra

characters.name: Traves

characters.description: A hostile former general whose castle becomes the target of Hadjar, Nero, and Serra. Their covert plan links him to the Ax Clan attacks on Hadjar.
characters.name: Larvie

characters.description: Hadjar's senior commander and protector. Although exhausted by war and missing her left arm, she recognizes Larvie's part in the assassination attempts and quietly gives Hadjar an alibi for acting against him.
characters.name: Leen
