recaps.ending: Black Gates is destroyed after Hadjar kills its patriarch, but the Moon Army pays for victory with immense losses. The cavalry commander dies stopping the sect's decay cloud. Hadjar survives gravely wounded, and the Neuronet functions that guided his final exchange will be unavailable for an estimated 1,754 days. He carries the patriarch's spatial ring but cannot open it. The island witch reveals herself as a white horned wolf, parts from Hadjar, and follows her own path. Nero, now Hadjar's blood brother, remains with Serra and chooses the capital over inheriting command. Hadjar accepts the end of his generalship and gives Leen's medallion to Leon, who leads fewer than 600,000 remaining Moon Army soldiers. Hadjar, Nero, Serra, Azrea, and the general staff messenger travel toward the capital under an order tied to Elaine's birthday and Hadjar's baronial retirement. Hadjar expects political danger from the summons. His hidden royal identity, Primus's rule, the unopened ring, the Lord of Nightmares' interest, and the two remaining tests and eventual price demanded by Traves all remain unresolved.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar and Nero build an elite unit, survive Larvie's attempt to kill them, and are drawn into a northern war. After Leen dies in a duel, Hadjar takes command, absorbs enemy defectors, captures a border city, and turns the army against Black Gates. He sacrifices an immortal inheritance to save the poisoned Nero, allies with mountain villagers, survives a vast beast migration, and commits himself permanently to the sword spirit. The Moon Army defeats Black Gates at Black Gorge, breaks the Snake Gates, and reaches the patriarch's stronghold. Hadjar kills the patriarch with help from the Neuronet, which then shuts down for years. The victory leaves the army shattered. The island witch departs after revealing her wolf form, Nero becomes Hadjar's blood brother, and Leon inherits command. Badly wounded and carrying an unopened spatial ring, Hadjar leaves with Nero, Serra, and Azrea for the capital, where Primus's court and Elaine's birthday summons await.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar survived the destruction of his royal family and lived under a concealed identity after his uncle Primus seized the throne of Lidus from Haver. The deeper cause of the conflict within the royal family remained unknown. Hadjar endured enslavement and later became a soldier, forming close bonds with the swordsman Nero and the caster Serra. His actions at Blue Wind Ridge earned him a reputation strong enough to draw other fighters to his banner. He also came into the care of Azrea, a white tiger cub, and carried a dragon heart whose residual guardian, Traves, subjected him to a larger path of tests and obligations. By the opening of this volume, Hadjar's public military rise offered a possible route back toward the palace, but it also placed him within reach of enemies connected to both the army and his hidden past.

So far this book: Hadjar and Nero train a thousand chosen recruits for the northern campaign, with Serra supporting the unit. An Ax Clan assassin reaches their camp and nearly kills Hadjar, but he defeats her and receives her speed-training scroll before her death. Hadjar also gains Moonbeam, a spirit-level sword. He, Nero, and Serra then plan a covert attack on Larvie, whose castle is tied to the assassination effort. Leen quietly provides an alibi while the trio uses a festival as cover. Inside the castle, Larvie completes an unnatural breakthrough with a scarlet stone and overwhelms Hadjar and Nero. Time stops when the Lord of Nightmares appears, identifies the stone as his demon heart, kills Larvie, and takes it. The overwhelmingly powerful being spares Hadjar and predicts that they will meet again. Hadjar and Nero escape as the castle collapses, but the encounter disables the Neuronet for four days and leaves Hadjar marked for an unknown future meeting.

Royal investigators pursue Larvie's death and begin abusing Hadjar's soldiers. Hadjar accepts fifty lashes in place of five men, then kills the responsible investigator in a lawful duel. A former Palace Guard leader recognizes him as the surviving prince, admits that Primus forced his part in the coup by threatening his family, and dies before explaining the old conflict involving Haver. Hadjar's unit grows dramatically before the northern march. At the border, Leen rejects surrender and faces her former fellow student and lover Darren in a customary duel. Darren mortally wounds her, and she gives Hadjar her general's medallion before dying. Hadjar immediately challenges Darren. During their fight he reaches one-with-the-world swordsmanship, defeats Darren, and receives the army's acclaim as its new general. The victory gives Hadjar the command he sought, but leaves him badly wounded as he inherits responsibility for Leen's soldiers.

Headquarters tries to replace Hadjar with an unqualified appointee, but the assembled army and commanders such as Leon defend his right to lead. Hadjar then accepts 200,000 enemy defectors who oppose their kingdom's enslavement and alliance with Black Gates. To solve his army's supply crisis, he crosses the border and uses leaflets, spies, and a coordinated uprising to seize a fortified city. He forbids indiscriminate looting and punishes soldiers who disobey, though sabotage continues after the capture. Hadjar declines to turn the campaign into a conquest of the neighboring capital. Instead, he announces that the enlarged Moon Army will destroy Black Gates. As the army approaches the sect's mountain pavilions, a Black Gates envoy arrives riding Stefa, a former circus ally who once aided Hadjar during his enslavement. She has been mutilated into an unresponsive human mount. After the envoy initiates violence, Hadjar kills him and ends Stefa's suffering. The act makes open war with the sect unavoidable and gives the campaign a deeply personal cost.

Hadjar prepares to seize the sixth Black Gates pavilion as a winter base. Simon solves a shortage of artillery crews by organizing ordinary recruits as gunners, while Serra builds a magical deception that draws the defenders toward their barrier. Ten thousand elite soldiers enter through the opening. During the assault, a pavilion master wounds Nero with a black halberd before Hadjar defeats him. The dying master summons an ancient tiger-like Defender, but Azrea confronts the creature and causes it to withdraw. The pavilion falls and Serra converts its barrier for the Moon Army, yet Nero's wound develops into a spreading black affliction. No healer or ordinary antidote can stop it. An imperial librarian identifies the attack as a patriarchal Black Gates technique and says that only a black stone flower can save Nero. The flower lies inside an ancient immortal's tomb that admits only young practitioners below the true-cultivator level. With Nero expected to die within days, Hadjar leaves his army and enters the mountains alone to find the cure.

Hadjar locates the buried immortal tomb and rejects an illusion in which his lost family lives, choosing Nero's rescue over the false reunion. He survives trials of will and endurance, then earns the right to choose between the dead swordsman's inheritance and the black stone flower. Hadjar takes the flower without hesitation. The tomb spirit rewards that choice with a subjective year of sword instruction compressed into one outside hour. Hadjar improves his fundamental skill and advances within the Formation stage, but again refuses to abandon Nero for the inheritance. After Hadjar departs, the spirit destroys the tomb and ends its own remnant existence. Elsewhere, Elaine seeks a portrait of General Hadjar and feels that she recognizes something in him, while Primus continues torturing the former royal nanny for the founder's sword. Hadjar returns in time. A healer processes the flower, removes the parasitic creature spreading through Nero's wound, and restores him to consciousness. Nero survives, though he still faces a long recovery.

With the sixth pavilion secured, Hadjar learns that the mountain villages expect a massive beast migration. He visits their defended settlement with trusted officers and meets Darius, who also warns him of an incurable black-fog disease associated with Black Gates. Darius sends Hadjar to an island-born witch who lives among wolves. She detects Azrea's scent and something deeper and unfamiliar within Hadjar. The witch then deceives him into believing he has been poisoned, using that fear to transfer his consciousness into a beast. Through the creature, Hadjar witnesses the approaching horde and its terror of a struggle between far stronger beasts. He returns to his own body weakened but convinced by what he witnessed. The invasion is real, and the Moon Army and neighboring settlements stand in its path.

Hadjar accepts the reality of the invasion but remains angry that the island witch risked his life to prove it. He promises Darius that the Moon Army will help defend the village in exchange for stored provisions, giving the army a food supply and the villagers a powerful ally. Darius estimates that the horde may arrive within two months. During Hadjar's recovery, he and the witch become lovers, though neither promises to abandon their own people or path. A Black Gates and Ax Clan assassin then attacks Hadjar to avenge a brother killed at the sixth pavilion. The stronger fighter wounds him repeatedly and escapes, leaving the threat unresolved. While recovering from the duel, Hadjar meditates at the local war-god statue and regains the sense of freedom he lost at Blue Wind Ridge. He advances into the Transformation stage and manifests a short-range sword cut driven by intention. Hadjar is stronger when he returns to command, but the assassin remains loose and the beast invasion is still approaching.

Hadjar's five hundred hunters kill ice bears and several white-ape groups while gathering cores for the planned fortress. The expedition culminates in an avalanche assault against hundreds of apes led by a gigantic fourth-stage alpha. Hadjar learns to redirect the creature's own force through his Calm Wind stance and kills it, though he suffers a serious leg wound. The mission costs twenty hunters in total and yields almost four hundred white-ape cores. The survivors give Hadjar the battlefield name Dragon. When the group returns, the escaped sect-clan assassin is holding the island witch as a hostage. She has deliberately allowed the situation to bring the assassin within Hadjar's reach. Hadjar attacks, and both men fall from a cliff. Hadjar survives and the assassin dies, ending the immediate vendetta. The witch and Hadjar renew their intimacy, while the army now possesses the cores needed to build its main defense against the approaching beast horde.

Over two months, the Moon Army turns the sixth pavilion into an ice fortress with artillery, layered walls, and shelters for the neighboring population. The beast horde arrives on an almost unmanageable scale, including thousands of alpha creatures and two beings too strong for the Neuronet to assess. Hadjar closes the gate while civilians are still outside and directs the defense. A flying beast destroys his tower and leaves him beyond the walls. Nero joins him, and the two hold the approach until Azrea transforms from a kitten into a giant white tigress and carries them back to safety. As the walls fail, Serra gathers the survivors beneath her barrier and unleashes fire and lightning that drive most of the horde onward. The army survives, but the region and its settlements are devastated. The island witch explains that Azrea's rescue consumed the reserve stored in her mother's core, so the transformation cannot presently be repeated. Black Gates has meanwhile abandoned its outer pavilions and concentrated at its central stronghold. With the Moon Army badly depleted, Hadjar calls a war council to decide the final campaign.

On the eve of the Black Gates campaign, Hadjar enters Traves's inner realm and faces the second of four tests attached to the dragon heart. Traves tests his mind through a chess-like battle. Hadjar succeeds by treating the pieces as soldiers whose lives place a duty on their commander. Offered a new technique, he chooses an irreversible path devoted entirely to the sword spirit, surrendering every other possible cultivation direction. Traves warns that two more dangerous tests remain and that the eventual price of the dragon heart is still concealed. In the river of world energy, the sword spirit strips away Hadjar's memories and repeatedly rejects him. He reconstructs his identity through sheer persistence and takes a single step toward it. The result expands his sword energy far beyond its former range and leaves a silver pattern of blades across his back. The island witch recognizes that the spirit has accepted and permanently changed him. Hadjar enters the coming war stronger, but bound to a path from which he cannot turn aside.

Black Gates threatens the residents of Black Gorge to force Hadjar into a trap. He enters the gorge alone while the Moon Army hides nearby, then attacks during the negotiation and signals the wider assault. The sect deploys a colossal bull carrying a fortified platform as its decisive weapon. Hadjar and Nero climb the beast, seize its fortification, and use explosives and sword strikes to destroy its eye and brain. With the bull dead, Hadjar faces the First Pavilion master. The master's wolf-shaped techniques cannot overcome Hadjar's new speed and sword energy, and Hadjar kills him before his final attack lands. The Moon Army wins at Black Gorge. Nero has fought beside Hadjar throughout the decisive action, while Leon, the cavalry, and the archers help contain the sect's strongest forces. The victory removes Black Gates' field commander and greatest beast weapon, but the sect's fortified entrance and patriarch remain ahead.

Hadjar, Nero, and Serra reconnoiter the Snake Gates and find immense walls protected by golems, rotating sickles, chained fire serpents, and aerial forces. Before the assault, Hadjar and Nero seal their friendship as blood brothers. Conventional attacks fail with heavy losses, so the island witch controls flocks of birds while Serra turns them into explosive distractions against the wyverns and walls. Adapted catapults launch Hadjar and Nero onto the parapet. They exploit the gate's own spinning blades to expose and destroy the golems' cores, plant charges on the sickle mechanisms, and leap to canvases held by soldiers below. The collapsing weapons smash the gates and bury the fire serpents. The Moon Army enters Black Gates territory through the breach. The central sect complex and its patriarch still stand, but the defensive structure thought to be impregnable has fallen.

Inside Black Gates, Hadjar kills two elite fighters while the allied forces break the remaining defenses. The sect releases a vast cloud of decay, and the cavalry commander leads tens of thousands into it, combining their strength to hold it back. He dies after saving the army. Hadjar then enters the patriarch's underground laboratory alone. A visiting Knight of Spirit departs with containers of epidemic black smoke after discussing the patriarch's forbidden work, including a pill made from one hundred thousand souls. The patriarch badly outmatches Hadjar and nearly kills him with inherited sickles and armed dead spirits. Hadjar breaks the artifact and wounds him, but survives the final exchange only by accepting the Neuronet forecast module's control. He kills the patriarch, and the Neuronet then shuts down for a projected 1,754 days. Hadjar takes an unfamiliar ring and leaves the cave gravely wounded. Black Gates is destroyed, its leader is dead, and Hadjar has survived the campaign, but the cost to both him and the Moon Army is immense.

In the aftermath, survivors rebuild the devastated valley and bury the dead. The island witch reveals that she is a white horned wolf from the islands. She and Hadjar accept that neither wants a shared domestic life, and they part on separate paths. Hadjar decides that his service as a general is over. A royal order summons him to the capital for Elaine's birthday and grants him a baronial title that effectively removes him from command. Nero declines the chance to inherit the army and chooses to accompany him. As the forces leave the mountains, the allied contingent returns home and fewer than 600,000 Moon Army soldiers continue. Hadjar seals a sword and spear in the border gorge as a memorial. Serra identifies the patriarch's ring as a spatial artifact, but no one can open it. Hadjar gives the general's medallion to Leon, making her commander of the Moon Army. Still badly wounded, he departs for the capital with Nero, Serra, Azrea, and Ralphie. He expects the royal summons to place him in political danger, while Traves's remaining tests, the Lord of Nightmares' interest, and the ring all remain unresolved.

recaps.ending: Nero persuades Hadjar to abandon revenge and leave Lidus with Serra and Elaine, but the Darnassus governor seals the palace and murders Nero. Serra enhances Moonbeam, destroys the governor and his remaining legionnaires with blue fire, and dies in the attack. Hadjar then defeats Primus, losing Moonbeam and suffering nearly fatal wounds. He restores Elaine's memories, but allows her attack to cast him into the lake so the kingdom can accept a public account in which the false prince died and Elaine became its rightful queen. Leen supports Elaine as military counselor, and Darnassus accepts her reign while appointing another governor. Elaine reforms the mines and forms the Northern Moon force with a neighboring kingdom. Azrea rescues Hadjar, who secretly reunites with Elaine before leaving Lidus. Carrying Serra and Aaron's wedding bracelets, he continues as Hadjar Traves and sets out to reach the gods' realm. Elaine keeps his survival secret and awaits his return.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar returns covertly to the Lidus capital, confronts Primus's oppressive rule, and learns that Nero is Crown Prince Aaron while Elaine is his own lost sister. A royal hunt leads Hadjar and Elaine to an ancient tree, where Elaine inherits the ancestral sword. After witnessing the mines' violence, she begins questioning the kingdom she knows. Hadjar infiltrates the northern rebels, hears Atticus's account of the coup and a demonic disaster, then kills him in a duel. Primus recognizes Hadjar and sentences him to burn, but the people and Moon Army rise in his defense. The Darnassus governor kills Nero, and Serra destroys the governor at the cost of her life. Hadjar kills Primus, restores Elaine's memories, and lets the world believe he dies so she can rule. Azrea rescues him. Elaine becomes queen and begins reforms, while Hadjar leaves with Azrea to seek the gods' realm.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar, the surviving son of the deposed King Haver, became a renowned general while concealing his royal identity. Primus, Hadjar's uncle, rules Lidus after the fall of Hadjar's family, and Darnassus holds decisive influence over the kingdom. Hadjar's path through war brought him close comrades, especially Nero and Serra, and made the Moon Army loyal to him. General Leen served as one of its senior commanders. Hadjar also gained Azrea, a young white tiger who travels as his companion. His victory over the Black Gates increased his fame but left his body and forming core badly strained. He now returns to the Lidus capital with his companions, carrying both a soldier's reputation and an unresolved claim against the ruler who replaced his father.

So far this book: Hadjar, Nero, Serra, and Ralphie enter the Lidus capital for Princess Elaine's birthday. Hadjar hides his former status as prince, but his fame as the victorious General Traves quickly draws attention. Still recovering from his Black Gates injuries, he defeats a hostile noble without relying fully on Moonbeam. Rowena then exposes his identity as the celebrated general to the tavern crowd. A walk through the poorer district brings Hadjar into conflict with a masked swordswoman after he refuses to intervene against abusive royal guards. Their clash, and Hadjar's own reflections, force him to confront how deeply war has exhausted his willingness to protect strangers. Playing music at the tavern restores some of his sense of purpose. Rowena then escorts Hadjar, Nero, and Serra across the capital. The sight of the palace after sixteen years leaves Hadjar preparing to enter the place bound to his family's overthrow.

So far this book: At court, Hadjar faces Primus while maintaining a false account of his origins. Elaine's arrival interrupts their veiled confrontation. Hadjar recognizes the princess as his lost younger sister, although she does not recognize him, and he keeps silent to protect her. She soon identifies him as the man who declined to help the civilians in the poor district and attacks him. Nero intervenes and reveals that he is actually Crown Prince Aaron, Primus's son and Elaine's brother. A blood oath had prevented him from explaining his identity, and his marriage to Serra further places him at odds with his father. Hadjar chooses to preserve their friendship. Later, on the abandoned palace training ground, Hadjar meets his aged childhood sword master. The instructor recognizes the surviving prince and secretly returns his loyalty, giving Hadjar a covert ally inside the palace while his identity remains hidden from Primus and Elaine.

So far this book: Primus grants Hadjar only a landless title and sends the royal youths on a politically charged hunt. Nero commands the party and makes Hadjar his deputy, but aristocrats trained by imperial schools resent the general. One challenges Hadjar to a duel. Hadjar withstands the nobleman's techniques and tries to end the contest without killing him. The defeated opponent instead attacks two servants, forcing Hadjar to protect them and accept wounds. Hadjar terrifies the noble into surrender but spares his life. At the Mountain of the Kings, earth dragons stampede the party. Elaine's horse carries her into a newly opened abyss, and Hadjar leaps after her while Nero is trapped above. The hunt's rivalry has now become a survival crisis, with Hadjar and Elaine missing beneath the mountain and the rest of the party unable to follow.

So far this book: Elaine awakens underground after Hadjar has spent days keeping her alive. The pair follow a submerged route out, battle a huge fish guarding the passage, and save one another from death before reaching impossibly ancient ruins. A powerful tree of life separates them into trials linked to an ancestral weapon. Hadjar gains a deeper understanding of his sword path but fails the tree's intended test because he continues seeking victory rather than accepting defeat and renouncing rule. Elaine succeeds in her own trial and receives the ancestral white sword, which is bound to her bloodline and can rest as a mark on her hand. The tree gives Hadjar a red leaf and an obscure warning about his eventual death. Hadjar intends to hide the tree and the valuable resources around it from the wider world.

So far this book: Elaine and Hadjar swear to conceal the tree of life and its resources. Elaine reveals missing childhood memories and old weapon scars, leading Hadjar to suspect deliberate interference. He takes her to a village whose residents describe forced labor at a mine she had been taught did not exist. Naila hosts them and becomes Elaine's first genuine friend beyond court. When mine troops raid the village, Elaine and Hadjar defeat them, but a dying soldier detonates an artifact that destroys the settlement. Hadjar saves Elaine while allowing the villagers to die, arguing that he cannot rescue people who will not act for themselves. Their moral divide remains unresolved. Nero and the search party finally arrive. Elaine executes the noble who had endangered servants during the earlier duel, then orders everyone back to the capital so she can confront Primus about the mine and the suffering concealed from her.

So far this book: On returning to the capital, Elaine admits responsibility for the noble's execution. Primus kills Duke Boreas when he seeks revenge and notices the mark of Elaine's ancestral sword. Hadjar remains under close watch, but he and Nero survive an attack by assassins connected to the dead duke. Nero and Serra marry with Hadjar as best man. During their wedding, Hadjar secretly assists an assassination attempt against Primus, using the confusion to wound the king before killing the attacker himself. A captured rebel denounces Primus as a usurper and names the lost prince as Lidus's true ruler. Primus responds by restoring Hadjar's rank as General Traves and assigning him to eliminate the rebels in the White Forest. The mission advances Hadjar's concealed revenge plan, even as the public challenge to Primus increases suspicion around the throne.

So far this book: Primus orders Hadjar to return within five weeks with the northern rebel leader's head, threatening a massive assault if he fails. Hadjar takes a small special-guard detachment into the White Forest, intending to use the soldiers as bait. Supernatural dangers, snow warriors, and attempted desertion steadily destroy the force. Azrea guides the survivors toward the hidden rebels. Their leader is Atticus, a former general and old friend of Haver who helped Primus seize power. Hadjar offers to join the rebellion and vows to kill Primus. When the royal lieutenant orders the cannons fired, rebel archers eliminate the escort. Atticus then transports Hadjar into the rebel camp and recognizes him as the missing prince. Hadjar has reached the force he meant to infiltrate, but he must now confront a man tied directly to his family's fall while his own identity is no longer secret inside the camp.

So far this book: Atticus explains that he, Haver, Primus, Elizabeth, and Leonora once faced a demonic incursion during war. A supernatural envoy called the disaster a heavenly error and required one woman to remain behind. Leonora sacrificed herself, leaving Primus grieving and Atticus indebted to him. Later, Primus planned to trade control of a valuable ore vein for Darnassus support and demanded Atticus's help removing Haver. A curse and prophecy prevented Atticus from escaping his assigned part. Atticus reveals that half a million northern rebels have waited to restore Hadjar. Hadjar nevertheless refuses reconciliation and duels him. Snowmen mortally wound Atticus, after which Hadjar completes their fight and kills him. Hadjar returns to Primus with Atticus's head and inherited dagger. The dagger exposes him as Hadjar Duran. Primus has him incapacitated and imprisoned in the dungeon where he suffered as a child.

So far this book: Primus suppresses Hadjar's cultivation and confines him with his former nanny, who has endured years of torture rather than disclose the route to the king's sword. At her request, Hadjar ends her suffering. Nero secretly brings Moonbeam and the means to escape, but Hadjar chooses to remain and face execution. As guards lead him to be burned, citizens cover his route with red flowers and officials quietly offer him painless poison. At the stake, Primus brands him a false prince. Hadjar rejects the public's passivity and calls on them to resist Darnassus and the king. A child answers first, then the crowd and executioner turn against the imperial forces. Leon arrives with the Moon Army and foreign allies. The real Moonbeam frees Hadjar from his collar. With his powers restored and the square in revolt, Hadjar leads the uprising toward the palace.

So far this book: The Moon Army, allied soldiers, palace guards, Hadjar's old sword master, and Azrea help break imperial control of the palace. Inside, Nero and Serra warn that killing Primus could bring Darnassus down on Lidus. Nero offers a different future in which he, Serra, Hadjar, and Elaine leave together. Hadjar accepts friendship over revenge. Before they can depart, the governor seals the palace, binds Primus, and reveals power far beyond what the court expected. He kills Nero from behind and turns his remaining warriors against Hadjar and Serra. Serra enhances Moonbeam with a spell that will soon destroy the weapon. She then unleashes blue fire that kills the governor and the surviving legionnaires while consuming her as well. Hadjar sends Leon and the Moon Army outside to secure the perimeter. Wounded and grieving Nero and Serra, he remains alone in the ruined palace with Primus for their final confrontation.

So far this book: Primus mourns Aaron before dueling Hadjar through the collapsing palace. Both are badly injured and exhaust their cultivation. Primus spends his remaining vitality on a final thrust, but Hadjar invokes the sword spirit and uses the last of Moonbeam to kill him. Elaine arrives under the mistaken belief that Hadjar murdered her father and attacks with the ancestral sword. Hadjar uses the tree's red leaf to restore her memories of Haver, Elizabeth, and her older brother. Rather than risk killing Elaine, he accepts her attack and falls into the lake below. Leen declares Elaine the rightful queen and Hadjar a dead false prince, securing the succession through the public story he intended. Darnassus accepts Elaine's rule under a new governor. She reforms the mines and creates the Northern Moon force with a neighboring kingdom. Azrea rescues Hadjar from the lake. He privately reconciles with Elaine, promises to return, and leaves Lidus with Azrea, Serra and Aaron's bracelets, and a new goal: reaching the gods' realm.

characters.name: Hadjar

characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.name: Azrea

characters.description: The dragon linked to Hadjar's heart who appears as a cultivation teacher in a vision. Before Hadjar's duel with a stronger tribal champion, Traves begins teaching him the Falling Leaf sword stance.

characters.name: Shakar

characters.name: Ilmena

characters.name: Serra

characters.name: Ilmena impostor

recaps.ending: Hadjar kills the Heaven Soldier commanding the caravan's western attackers, exposing the supposed bandits as troops of the desert king. The victory immediately collapses when an illusionist who has replaced Ilmena murders the caravan owner, seizes Serra, and calls a sand dragon. The dying owner identifies Serra as an ancient magical key tied to a library and asks Hadjar to use the sought elixir to make her human. Hadjar consumes the body of a divine messenger in a desperate response. A black-armored manifestation drives back the dragon, and Einen removes the exhausted Hadjar through shadow to Underworld City. Both arrive injured, Einen unconscious and Hadjar subject to the city's judgment. The real Ilmena's fate is unknown. The caravan's expedition toward Mage City has lost its leader, and its survivors' position is unstated. The desert king's daughter delivers Serra to her father, whose army continues its conquests and whose ambition is immortality or godhood. Serra remains captive as Hadjar wakes in Underworld City calling her name.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar joins a caravan crossing the Sea of Sand and forms a durable partnership with Einen. After raids, a tribal duel, and the defense of a sentient oasis, Hadjar earns the name Darkhan, gains the sword Mountain Wind, and masters a brief call upon his Dark Storm dragon inheritance. The caravan owner then reveals a hidden expedition to Mage City for a legendary god-making elixir and forces the guards to participate. During an attack by soldiers disguised as bandits, an illusionist posing as Ilmena kills the owner, abducts Serra, and summons a sand dragon. A Black General-linked manifestation repels the dragon, while Einen carries the exhausted Hadjar to Underworld City. The illusionist is the desert king's daughter, and Serra remains her father's captive as Hadjar awakens far away calling for her.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar is a Lydian fugitive and swordsman traveling toward the Empire. He carries the bracelets of dead companions and remains affected by those losses. Azrea travels with him and acts as a check when anger or revenge threatens his judgment. The dragon Traves is linked to Hadjar's heart and serves as a source of cultivation guidance. These ties and unresolved burdens accompany Hadjar as he approaches the Sea of Sand.

Hadjar reaches a border town seeking affordable passage across the Sea of Sand toward the Empire. He enters a difficult guard selection run by Shakar, the caravan's Heaven Soldier security chief. Shakar's nephew Shakh, the lightning-fast dagger fighter Ilmena, and a shadow-wielding islander are the other finalists. Hadjar defeats Shakh after a dangerous duel, while the islander wins the first available position. The islander later introduces himself as Einen and displays an ability to hide even from Hadjar and Azrea's senses. Hadjar and Einen agree to travel as companions. When two guards disappear, Shakar also takes Ilmena into the force. The recruits join a caravan of more than a thousand travelers. They receive security and welfare duties in its central section, meet vanguard leader Kharad, and see the caravan's exceptionally powerful elderly owner. At sunset the expedition leaves the pass and enters the Sea of Sand for a journey expected to last three years.

A month into the crossing, Hadjar and Einen suspect that the caravan command is hiding a major danger. A wanted portrait exposes Hadjar as General Hadjar Traves of Lidus, believed dead and sought by the Empire. Rather than claim the reward, the caravan leaders ask for his military advice. They explain that desert forces are converging on the route as Prince Sankesh advances toward Mage City. Hadjar and Einen join Kharad's scouts with Ilmena and Shakh. Learning that hundreds of bandits block the route, the four infiltrate their camp. Hadjar recognizes its strongest fighter as a former mercenary who tortured him in childhood. Azrea stops him from killing the defeated man in helpless rage, and Hadjar instead allows an armed final exchange before killing him. The group destroys the camp and frees its captives. When Ilmena and Shakh object that the caravan cannot support them, Hadjar gives up his share of the spoils so they can purchase passage. The raid ends with the captives supplied and Hadjar's companions forced to reconsider him.

Hadjar follows a hidden map from his former tormentor's grave and opens an artifact-sealed cache containing wealth and a king-stage monster core. His group uses captured oasis frogs to reach the Dead Mountains, where they rejoin Kharad and enter negotiations with a powerful Bedouin tribe. Kharad offers supplies, valuables, and enslaved people for passage. When the tribal leader demands Azrea, Hadjar refuses to regard her as property and proposes a duel instead, staking his freedom and the caravan's route on the outcome. Einen reveals that his own father operated a slave fleet, but Hadjar does not hold him responsible for his father's actions. In a vision before the duel, Traves teaches Hadjar the Falling Leaf stance and helps him change how he carries memories of his past. Hadjar then faces the tribe's Heaven Soldier champion, Coyote, whose spinning blades and movement through sand leave him badly wounded. Hadjar's new techniques allow him to fight back, but a clash sends stone toward a young spectator. He shields the child, suffering critical wounds while the duel's result remains unsettled.

Hadjar finds a rich cache left by his former tormentor, including a king-stage monster core. At the Dead Mountains, the caravan negotiates with a Bedouin tribe by offering goods and enslaved people. When the tribal leader shows interest in Azrea, Hadjar refuses to treat her as property and stakes his freedom in a duel for passage. Traves begins teaching him the Falling Leaf stance in a vision. Hadjar remains outmatched by the tribe's Heaven Soldier champion, Coyote, but abandons a possible victory to shield a child from flying stone. The tribe accepts him for that choice, and its shaman gives him the name Darkhan and a protective mark. Hadjar later uses the monster core to awaken his spirit. At the next oasis, a thief and a magical current carry him onto a forbidden plateau. There he meets Ignis, the sentient being who is the oasis, forest, and pond. Ignis kills a divine spy that had followed Hadjar. Unable to attack mortals under ancient restrictions, she temporarily transforms Hadjar's sword and asks him to defend the settlement from an approaching bandit army.

A vast bandit army led by a Spirit Knight attacks the oasis. Its commander claims the sheikh has taken something from him, but the ruler refuses to appear. Enemy bombardment breaches the magical barrier, and Hadjar and Einen join the defenders outside it. Ignis's enchantment lets Hadjar's ordinary sword strike with the force of an imperial weapon. Einen helps him kill a giant Heaven Soldier, then prevents battle rage from overwhelming him. With the defenders steadily losing to the enemy Spirit Knight, Hadjar organizes their remaining Heaven Soldiers around a single opening. He reaches for an echo of his sword spirit and launches a dragon-shaped attack despite wounds that leave him near collapse. His three-part Falling Leaf strike breaks through the commander's layered defenses without killing him. The oasis sheikh then reveals his own Spirit Knight power and finishes the wounded attacker with an arrow. The siege ends, but Hadjar is severely injured and his exhausted sword breaks after Ignis's temporary enhancement fades.

Hadjar survives the oasis battle. Sheikh Umar, the oasis ruler and a former student of the caravan owner, forgives his forbidden ascent because of his service but orders him to leave. As compensation, Umar permits one choice from his treasury. Ignis guides Hadjar to a heavy heaven-level sword, later called Mountain Wind, and Einen extracts him before Umar can intervene. Ignis then recognizes Hadjar as a descendant of the Black General and turns against him, though she cannot act beyond the oasis. Outside the settlement, Einen explains inherited nonhuman blood and reveals his own pearl-trout lineage. Hadjar admits that his inheritance comes from a dragon. With Einen prepared to kill him if he loses control, Hadjar enters a ritual dream to confront Traves. The dragon recounts the destruction of his Dark Storm village and tests Hadjar against the merciless strength of his former self. Hadjar cannot overpower him directly, but persists through devastating attacks and finds a way to wound the trial figure. Traves declares the test won and accepts Hadjar into the Dark Storm tribe.

Hadjar awakens from the inheritance trial with a Dark Storm mark over his heart. Traves teaches him to keep the dragon call secret. With Einen's help, Hadjar learns to sustain its power for only a few seconds, gaining greatly increased movement and striking force. The pair rejoin the caravan. A living Serra gives Hadjar a warm pink pebble and briefly speaks with an adult manner, while Einen warns that her apparent father treats her as valuable property. The caravan owner summons Hadjar and Einen and finally reveals the expedition's concealed purpose. Its route bends toward Mage City, where a legendary elixir is said to turn its drinker into a god. The owner's account says the elixir was created to free a woman imprisoned by the god of war, though the story remains only a legend. When the guards resist, the owner incapacitates them and uses Black Gates poison and its antidote as leverage. Hadjar, Einen, and the others submit under duress. Roughly three hundred people will join the year-long venture, and the owner reserves the elixir for himself.

Hadjar and Einen suspect that the caravan owner's explanation conceals further plans. Before they can investigate, more than three thousand supposed bandits approach. The caravan forms a fortified camp, and Hadjar and Einen take the exposed western flank. They cut through the mounted attackers until a wind-using Heaven Soldier stops Hadjar. The opponent reveals himself as an officer of the desert king, proving that regular troops are hidden among the raiders. Badly wounded and nearly empty of energy, Hadjar briefly invokes his dragon heart, destroys an autonomous dagger artifact, and ultimately kills the officer with a new understanding of his bond with the sword. The caravan routs the remaining attackers, but the apparent victory is a trap. An illusionist has replaced Ilmena. She kills the caravan owner, abducts Serra, and summons a sand dragon. Dying, the owner identifies Serra as an ancient magical key connected to a library and asks Hadjar to use the gods' elixir to make her human. Hadjar swallows the dead divine messenger's body and releases a column of black energy as the dragon arrives.

Hadjar's desperate act draws him into childhood memory, where Queen Elizabeth is confirmed as his mother and tells a tale linking a black-armored general to divine powers. In a separate vision, Hadjar encounters an overwhelming scarred figure with a black sword. At the caravan fortification, a black-armored manifestation emerges from the energy column and drives back the summoned sand dragon. Einen risks himself to pull the exhausted Hadjar away through shadow. They arrive badly injured at Underworld City. A red-haired disciple of the city's sage tries to kill the unconscious Hadjar, but an official stops her and takes both strangers inside. Einen remains unconscious, while Hadjar is detained under the sage's authority. Elsewhere, the desert king's army conquers and destroys a fortified city. The illusionist who replaced Ilmena is revealed as the king's daughter and presents Serra to him as the captured key. The king seeks immortality or godhood and retains Serra despite her warning that Hadjar will kill him. Hadjar awakens in Underworld City calling Serra's name. The true Ilmena's fate, the broken Mage City expedition, and Serra's rescue remain unresolved.

characters.name: Serra

characters.name: Tilis

characters.name: Karissa

characters.name: Glen

characters.name: Paris

characters.name: Arcus

characters.name: Black General

characters.name: Servant boy

characters.name: Sankesh

characters.name: Harlim

characters.description: A past ruler of the Pearl of the Sands. Ramukhan identifies Serra as his granddaughter while questioning Hadjar about what Rahaim disclosed.
characters.name: Rahaim

characters.description: The hardened leader of the surviving caravan remnant. Able to disperse into sand, he abducts Hadjar and accuses him of betraying the caravan's contract.
characters.name: Shakh

characters.description: Shakh's uncle and the caravan's former security chief. Mortally wounded and missing an arm, a leg, and an eye, he tells the survivors that Hadjar could not have betrayed their contract.
characters.name: Shakar

characters.description: The former head scout of Rahaim's caravan and one of its few survivors. He remains wary of Hadjar after the caravan's destruction.
characters.name: Kharad

characters.description: A caravan scout among the depleted group of survivors led by Shakh. He is present when Hadjar and Einen are brought into their hidden camp.
characters.name: Sular

characters.description: A former caravan guard whose body was found by the survivors in a wagon controlled by Sankesh's daughter. Her death is part of the disaster that shattered the caravan.
characters.name: Ilmena

characters.description: Serra's bodyguard and the keeper responsible for her as Mage City's living key. He publicly posed as her father and was lost after confronting Sankesh.
characters.name: Zerk

characters.description: A warrior and emissary who meets the Underworld City expedition near the suspected Mage City region. She invites Hadjar to enter Sankesh's camp and speak with him alone.
characters.name: Sankesh's daughter

characters.description: A northern heaven soldier ordered by Sankesh to issue a formal duel challenge to Hadjar under the laws of hospitality.
characters.name: Northern duelist

characters.name: Traves

characters.name: Black ancestral entity

characters.description: Sankesh as the commander of a brutal northern expedition. More than five hundred followers have been reduced to ten, yet he continues toward Mage City's library with Serra injured and captive.
characters.name: Northern konung

characters.description: The surviving memory of an ancient figure who meets Hadjar in an isolated cloud realm. She identifies him as a descendant of her enemy and links his blood and soul-bound sword to the Black General.
characters.name: Ancient sorceress

characters.name: Library golem

characters.description: The original name of the childlike golem who catalogs Mage City's library. She creates a helper for each seeker and warns that the northern force will arrive within minutes.
characters.name: List

characters.description: The northern force's head of security, left behind to prevent Hadjar and Einen from following his leader deeper into the library. His Spirit Knight strength makes him a severe obstacle for both men.
characters.name: Northern spirit knight

characters.name: Aril

characters.description: An enslaved girl sold at a northern auction after her mother is killed. A village chief purchases her with the boy he renames Aril and makes him responsible for her welfare.
characters.name: Aisha

characters.description: The name Aril uses after years of solitary survival and a rapid rise through sun cultivation. He returns to the village with overwhelming strength and learns that Aisha died giving birth to their daughter.
characters.name: Sunshine

characters.description: The daughter of the Green Hammer sect patriarch. She observes Hadjar and Einen when they arrive outside Holy Sky School.
characters.name: Dora Marnil

recaps.ending: Hadjar reaches the collapsing library's power complex alone, survives an apparently fatal blow, and advances to heaven soldier. Unable to defeat Sankesh directly, he destroys the crystals sustaining the flying island and shatters the god-making elixir. Sankesh's memories reveal how abandonment by Rahaim, enslavement, Aisha's suffering, and the loss of their daughter shaped his pursuit of absolute strength. When that purpose fails, his cultivation path breaks and he dies. Serra uses her power as the library's key to expel Hadjar before the island explodes, remaining behind after placing one elixir drop in his ring. Einen's group finds Hadjar three weeks later. They return to Underworld City, where the sage identifies himself as the real Rahaim and explains the disastrous choice made by his golem. He also confirms that Hadjar's incomplete soul prevents him from using the true path of cultivation. Hadjar still carries the Black General's inheritance, the dragon-heart debt, and his House of Blade Fury oath. Rahaim's promised reward sends Hadjar and Einen to Holy Sky School, opening their next search for advancement and knowledge of the immortals.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar and Einen survive captivity beneath Underworld City and join a dangerous expedition to Mage City's lost library. Traveling with mistrustful specialists, they cross the Sea of Sand, encounter surviving allies and enemies, and use Serra's stone to penetrate the city's defenses. Inside the library, Glen betrays the party to Sankesh, whose pursuit of a god-making elixir grew from abandonment, enslavement, and the loss of Aisha. Hadjar advances to heaven soldier, destroys the elixir and the island's power, and survives when Serra sacrifices herself to send him away with one remaining drop. Sankesh dies as his cultivation path collapses. Back in Underworld City, the sage reveals himself as the true Rahaim and explains that Hadjar's incomplete soul blocks the true cultivation path. Rahaim rewards Hadjar and Einen with recommendations to Holy Sky School, where they arrive at the close.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar traveled with Einen and the tigress Azrea. Serra had become important to Hadjar, and his journey had also bound his fate to a dragon and to questions about powers beyond ordinary cultivation. A passage through a spatial rift ended the previous stage of the journey and separated the companions from familiar ground.

Hadjar awakens after three weeks in an energy-draining prison beneath Underworld City, immobilized beside Einen. Azrea escaped when they arrived, but neither man knows where she has gone. A city official rejects Hadjar's attempt to invoke Serra's name and says Tilis seeks revenge for Serra's death. Servants led by Salif release the prisoners only to collar, bridle, and march them deeper into the settlement. Hadjar and Einen establish that their captors need them alive, but an attempted reversal earns them further punishment. Karissa then presents the captured outsiders with three compulsory forms of service: decades as servants, years in the mines, or one dangerous year in the research chamber. Hadjar and Einen both select the research path, accepting its risks in exchange for eventual citizenship, freedom, and the return of their belongings.

The research bracelets permit Hadjar and Einen to use power but punish any intention to harm a city resident. In the blue barracks, they recover their withheld weapons and refuse Glen's authority, leaving them isolated among hostile residents. Hadjar defeats an emerald wolf in his first pit trial, while Einen survives a giant beetle. Principal researcher Paris measures both men at yellow talent and suggests that the city's sage alone could teach the true cultivation path. Their small wages prove inadequate for the techniques sold at auction, and Tilis reinforces her belief that Hadjar caused Serra's disappearance. Paris offers a way out of routine arena service: field expeditions into the Sea of Sand, where specimens and artifacts might bring both resources and freedom. Hadjar and Einen accept, hoping the assignment will also lead to knowledge and escape. When they return to the barracks, however, Hadjar finds Einen tortured and collared by Glen's faction. Glen surrounds Hadjar and tries to force the confrontation the newcomers had previously avoided.

Hadjar answers Glen's attack by killing most of the barracks faction before Karissa uses the slave bracelets to halt the fight. After treating Einen's injuries, the pair spend two months surviving pit battles and preparing for field work. Paris then assembles a deeply divided expedition: Hadjar, Einen, Glen, Karissa, Salif and his young companion, plus Ramukhan and Tilis. Their objective is Mage City's lost library, whose location may become accessible when two red comets converge. Sankesh's competing force, altered beasts, ancient traps, and regions that suppress projected techniques all threaten the search. Each participant bargains for payment. Hadjar secures removal of his restraint and a future audience with the sage, while Einen asks for cores and artifact access. Paris assigns roles based on the travelers' abilities: Salif will preserve maps, Glen will track, Ramukhan and Tilis will manage spells, and Hadjar and Einen will cover conditions that limit conventional magic. Azrea returns before departure, but distrust remains central to the group, especially between the two companions and Glen.

The expedition leaves Underworld City and enters the Sea of Sand under Ramukhan's command. In the black sands of the Demon's Heart, Hadjar, Einen, and Glen fight powerful beasts. Hadjar develops Falling Leaf and briefly draws on dragon blood to kill a scorched falcon, only for a wounded dragon to appear. Harlim, an Immortal of the House of Golden Heavens, intervenes and removes the encounter from everyone else's memory. He tells Hadjar that his former shadow-master faces judgment and leads him into a blood oath: Hadjar must honor that master through the House of Blade Fury or lose his soul. Harlim also warns against the reputed god-making elixir and privately redirects the search to Stone Trees Oasis. Hadjar later tells Einen what was erased. At the oasis, Ramukhan reveals that Rahaim once ruled the Pearl of the Sands and calls Serra Rahaim's granddaughter. Hadjar withholds his suspicion that Serra is more than human and may be Mage City's key. While he meditates alone, an unknown attacker accompanied by a sand dog disarms and captures him.

Hadjar's captor is Shakh, now leader of the few survivors from Rahaim's caravan. The devastated group believes Hadjar betrayed them, but the mortally wounded Shakar insists that he could not have broken the contract. The survivors explain that Ilmena was found dead, the caravan was destroyed amid a clash between a black spirit and a dragon, and Sankesh later overwhelmed what remained. They also reveal that Serra is alive and serves as a living map, guide, and key connected to Mage City. After Shakar dies, Shakh gives Hadjar Rahaim's letter. Einen recognizes it as a cipher-map, and the two groups agree to cooperate while concealing the meeting from the Underworld City party. Hadjar then attempts a dangerous advancement. Karissa, Tilis, and Ramukhan contain and hide the power released by his internal struggle. He succeeds in reaching the new soul stage, gains sharper perception of energy, and removes the dissonance from Mountain Wind. His improved strike demonstrates power far beyond what the surrounding practitioners expect from his nominal stage.

Einen reveals the decoded map to the expedition and swears that it is genuine. The party follows it toward ruins in the likely Mage City region, where Sankesh's daughter invites Hadjar to meet her father alone. Hadjar enters a camp holding hundreds of heavily equipped soldiers and learns that Sankesh knows his past as a general of Lidus and a kingslayer. Sankesh offers to remove Hadjar's restraint, accelerate his advancement, and give him military command. Hadjar rejects both the offer and Sankesh's belief that strength should determine who deserves to live. Bound by hospitality from killing his guest outright, Sankesh orders a northern heaven soldier to challenge Hadjar. The duelist uses ice, a blizzard, and strong artifacts to wound and obscure himself from Hadjar. Drawing on perception, prior training against Einen, and the wind and snow around him, Hadjar forces out the true opponent and kills him with Falling Leaf. Sankesh then tries to strike the exhausted victor, but his own followers enforce the rules of hospitality. Hadjar leaves gravely wounded and marked for pursuit.

Einen retrieves the badly wounded Hadjar, who reports the scale of Sankesh's army and his belief that Serra is hidden nearby. During unconscious visions, Hadjar rejects an offer to abandon his ambitions and instead renews his determination to seek justice and reach the seventh heaven. His clues point the expedition toward a lake covered by fog at night. While incapacitated, he meets Traves, the dragon fragment bound to his soul, and develops Rustle in the Treetops as a defensive Light Breeze stance. Traves is then confronted by a black ancestral entity linked to Hadjar's inner sword and bloodline. After waking, Hadjar helps select a western lake protected by an anomaly that ignores mortals. Salif's young companion scouts it while magically disguised and finds a passage beneath the false bottom. Karissa prepares an ability-sealing potion so the practitioners can cross. Before entering, they take blood oaths against harming one another. Salif, the boy, and the sleeping Azrea remain at camp, while Hadjar, Einen, Glen, Karissa, Ramukhan, and Tilis descend through the lake into a concealed desert.

Inside the hidden desert, Einen reveals that he falsified his blood oath and quietly prepared safeguards against the other expedition members. A Spirit Knight-level sand creature nearly destroys the group until Hadjar, Einen, Karissa, Tilis, and Ramukhan coordinate their different powers. Ramukhan spends one of the sage's two seals to eliminate a second creature. Hadjar then heals Glen's damaged meridians, although Ramukhan's control of the blue bracelets exposes the limits of their supposed equality. Comparing the slain spirit's core with Serra's stone strengthens Hadjar's conclusion that Serra is a constructed being tied to Mage City. He also breaks the seal on the Black Gates patriarch's spatial ring and finds dangerous medicines, poison, wealth, and an ancient image of a black swordsman. Mage City's guardians annihilate another camp, while Serra's stone seems to guide Hadjar's party safely around further defenses. The travelers finally reach artificial mountains surrounding a hidden center. An unseen examiner recognizes Darkhan, questions Hadjar's priorities, and subjects the group to three riddles. Their answers dissolve the enclosing walls, clearing the first threshold into Mage City.

An ancient golem admits the seekers to Mage City's citadel because one of them bears a Name. Sankesh's force, reduced to ten survivors, follows with Serra as a wounded captive. At the gates, Serra's stone protects the party and Hadjar's voice opens the way, but an ancient sorceress's memory separates him from the others. She identifies him as a descendant of the Black General and confirms that the General's sword exists within his soul. Hadjar refuses an offered escape and instead witnesses a memory of Mage City's fall, though the General's true identity remains unresolved. The memory gives him a blue plate, which works with Serra's stone to reveal the library entrance. After surviving collapsing stairs, enchantments, moving platforms, and lethal guardians, the party reaches the library proper. A childlike golem introduces herself as Serra's sister, then gives her name as List. With Sankesh minutes away, she offers each seeker assistance. The knowledge Hadjar wants has been destroyed, so he chooses an ancient tablet teaching meditation on the sword spirit and begins studying the Black General's image.

Sankesh and his remaining fighters enter the library with captive Serra. He demands the divine elixir and another lost technique, then tortures List when she cannot provide them. Glen betrays Hadjar at knife point, but Einen wounds Glen and reveals Shakh's concealed allies. Sankesh takes Serra and List deeper into the complex while his northern head of security blocks pursuit. Serra calls Sankesh her younger brother, and his memories show that he is Rahaim's abandoned son. Rahaim once chose to rescue Serra after both children were captured, leaving the boy in slavery. The library fight divides. Shakh and his scouts engage Sankesh's daughter and her soldiers, while Hadjar and Einen struggle against the northern spirit knight. Sular and Kharad are killed, but Shakh decapitates Sankesh's daughter. Einen advances to the spear-wielder stage during the continuing battle. With direct attacks still failing, he positions three power-bearing artifact stones over the enemy. Hadjar breaks them open, causing a massive release of energy that kills the spirit knight and destroys the library hall. Hadjar shields Tilis from the collapse and falls critically wounded.

Einen uses a rare extract to close Hadjar's worst wounds. Tilis accepts Hadjar's account that he did not kill Serra, but the surviving party is nearly unable to fight: its spellcasters have lost their principal artifacts, Shakh is badly injured, and the library island will soon collapse. Hadjar decides that Sankesh must be stopped from obtaining the elixir. When Einen refuses to leave him, Hadjar knocks his friend unconscious and sends the group toward the escape seal. In the power complex, Hadjar finds Serra alive beside a dying fellow golem. Sankesh nearly cuts Hadjar in half and destroys Mountain Wind, but Hadjar survives the apparent death and advances to heaven soldier. His black sword can now manifest physically, allowing him to contend with the much more experienced Spirit Knight. Under repeated attacks, Hadjar creates a new movement stance called Wind and begins wounding Sankesh, though he cannot overcome the enemy's strengthened body. Instead, he destroys the crystals supporting the flying island. A fragment of Mountain Wind breaks the final crystal and the elixir's shell. The vessel shatters, the elixir spills across crystal fragments, and the entire island begins to fall.

The shattered elixir forces Sankesh to relive the purpose behind his pursuit of strength. As a boy, he was taken from the Sea of Sand and sold in the North. A village chief purchased him with Aisha, renamed him Aril, and made him responsible for her. They later became lovers, but a visiting leader's son assaulted Aisha while Aril was beaten for trying to intervene. When Aisha became pregnant, Aril abandoned her. He survived alone, found sun-cultivation teachings, and returned with power, only to learn that Aisha had died giving birth to their daughter. His later campaign and search for the elixir grew from a desire to create a world where strength would prevent such exploitation and separation. Faced with the elixir's ruin, he recognizes the failure of that path. His halberd spirit cracks, his cultivation collapses, and he dies. Serra then uses her nature as the library's key to force Hadjar away from the falling island. She remains behind, but secretly leaves one drop of elixir in his spatial ring. Hadjar survives the explosion and resolves to return to Underworld City.

Three weeks after Mage City's destruction, Einen's party finds Hadjar. The survivors take another month to return to Underworld City, where Hadjar demands the audience promised before the expedition. The city's sage reveals that he is the real Rahaim, an ancient lord who left a golem in the Pearl of the Sands to manage the search for the library and care for Serra and his son. That substitute chose Serra when both children were captured, beginning the chain of abandonment and loss that shaped Sankesh. Rahaim also explains that the prophetic image of a dragon consuming the sun concerned the conflict between Hadjar and Sankesh. When he tests Hadjar's new ability to draw on external energy, he finds a fundamental obstacle: Hadjar's soul is incomplete, preventing him from following the true cultivation path despite his advancement to heaven soldier. As the expedition's reward, Rahaim gives Hadjar and Einen recommendations to Holy Sky School in the imperial capital. The two companions arrive at the school's gates, still seeking advancement and knowledge about the land of the immortals.

characters.description: A heaven soldier and seasoned survivor who travels beside Einen. With Rahaim's recommendation in hand, he intends to enter the Holy Sky School and find a path beyond its lowest rank.
characters.name: Hadjar

characters.description: The name linking Hadjar to the ancient spirit identified by Helmer as his ancestor.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.description: Hadjar's trusted travelling companion, now a true cultivator. His unusual eyes can see through shadows, and he approaches the Holy Sky School examination with the same practical caution and willingness to share danger that define his partnership with Hadjar.
characters.name: Einen

characters.description: An ally from Underworld City who chooses a separate road when Hadjar and Einen depart. Carrying Ilmena's ribbon, he plans to visit the families of those who died, tell her parents that she loved them, and then continue travelling independently.
characters.name: Shock

characters.description: A young heir of the Predatory Blades clan who provokes Hadjar during the entrance examination. He carries an imperial sword artifact, has at least middle heaven-soldier strength, and treats an idle observation from Hadjar as an insult demanding submission.
characters.name: Predatory Blades heir

characters.description: The Holy Sky School's ninth-ranked disciple and a middle-stage spirit knight. As an inner-circle examiner, he subjects the ordinary applicants to overwhelming pressure, eliminating nearly the entire group before the remaining admission tests begin.
characters.name: Dalit

characters.description: A young spirit knight who accompanies the hostile Predatory Blades heir during the school examination. Her position beside him and her evident cultivation mark her as more than a ceremonial servant, but her personal circumstances are not yet explained.
characters.name: Predatory Blades attendant

characters.description: The low-ranked Predatory Blades clan heir previously encountered by Hadjar and Einen during the school entrance examination.
characters.name: Tom

characters.description: The spirit knight first presented as Tom's attendant. Dora identifies her as Tom's sister and indicates that their position within the Predatory Blades clan is complicated.
characters.name: Tom's sister

characters.description: A Holy Sky School examiner who recognizes Hadjar during the final admission test. Behind his official position, he privately covets Hadjar's name as an ingredient for a Hundred Voices pill, making his interest in the new disciple covertly predatory.
characters.name: Markin

characters.description: The Holy Sky School mentor who formally admits Hadjar and Einen as ordinary disciples after they pass the entrance examination.
characters.name: Jean

characters.description: An ancient golem who guards the Treasure Tower and controls entry to its resources.
characters.name: Treasure Tower keeper

characters.description: A physically formidable ordinary disciple who has spent years at the school and leads an organized demand for newcomers' starting glory points. When Hadjar and Einen refuse to pay for his information and protection, he makes them targets for his group.
characters.name: Ordinary-disciple extortionist

characters.description: A powerful elf with a peak heaven-soldier aura and an imperial hammer artifact. She intercepts Hadjar and Einen after their exhausting fight with the extortionists, offering knowledge about elves while making clear that she has business involving them.
characters.name: Dora

characters.description: The figure associated with the dangerous sword power Hadjar inherited before this journey.
characters.name: Black General

characters.description: Hadjar's established dragon mentor from his earlier journeys.
characters.name: Traves

characters.description: An ordinary disciple and servant of House Tarez who seeks information about Hadjar and Einen. His inquiries continue the retaliation prompted by the death of another house servant, identifying him as the next active agent of that feud.
characters.name: Ian Gore

characters.description: A demon emissary who enters a shadow barrier to meet Hadjar in private. Hadjar deliberately seeks information from him, but Einen warns that any bargain with such a figure is dangerous, and Helmer's interest makes the exchange more than a simple consultation.
characters.name: Helmer

characters.description: A fully-fledged Meltwater School disciple who duels Hadjar during the Imperial Road battle. Though better equipped and more advanced in cultivation, he withdraws after Hadjar damages his armor, salutes him as a worthy opponent, and promises to finish their contest another time.
characters.name: Meltwater School opponent

characters.description: A long-lived lord at the Holy Sky School who approaches Hadjar privately. He says that cultivation took him far from his homeland and may offer Hadjar a special task if the disciple earns a gold token.
characters.name: Long-lived school mentor

characters.description: The commander of an airborne elven guard force who answers Dora's distress signal after the Imperial Road battle. She arrives on a griffin to retrieve her sister, commands powerful house guards, and refuses to extend their aid to the other wounded disciples.
characters.name: Dora's elder sister

characters.description: A great-clan swordsman whom Hadjar recognizes as an earlier battlefield opponent. He seeks a future duel conducted on fair terms, and his encounter with Dora's group at an elite capital restaurant presents him as a proud rival rather than an immediate enemy.
characters.name: Young noble swordsman

characters.description: An armored spirit knight with a massive sword who commands the final stage of the attack on Dora. She confronts Hadjar inside the sealed garden and offers an antidote for his poisoned companions only if he defeats her, while confirming Dora remains her assigned target.
characters.name: Female spirit-knight assassin

characters.description: A talking raven encountered while Hadjar is unconscious. It is the same raven seen with the assassin and claims that Hadjar is its descendant.
characters.name: Raven-form ancestor

characters.description: An exceptionally powerful healer from Dora's family who removes Einen's poison and improves his damaged energy channels. When she examines Hadjar, she finds a grave wound to his soul and an ancient force that violently repels her attempt to investigate it.
characters.name: Elf healer

characters.description: An elf warrior and the healer's niece who is present while the elves treat Hadjar's dangerous condition.
characters.name: Inora

characters.description: The ruler of Dora's elven house and brother of the healer. Convinced that the ancient force inherited by Hadjar poses an existential danger, he prepares to execute Hadjar despite the healer's argument that a descendant still has independent will.
characters.name: Elf ruler

characters.description: Jean's old friend, a middle-stage lord and swordsman capable of forming a sword kingdom. After thirty years of secluded meditation, he has no interest in taking a personal disciple until Jean describes Hadjar's unusually early attainment of the Sword's Heart.
characters.name: Elder sword mentor

characters.description: Hadjar's lightning-charged tigress companion, who intervenes to guard him after he collapses unconscious in the arena.
characters.name: Lightning tigress

characters.description: An initial-stage lord who commands the warship Rook's Wings. His vessel gives Hadjar passage toward Fort Derrigan on the western border, allowing the disciple to travel under military authority while undertaking the elder sword mentor's retrieval mission.
characters.name: Viscount Abrax

characters.description: A scarred initial-stage spirit knight and senior crewman aboard Rook's Wings. He is openly skeptical that a Holy Sky School disciple will serve capably as an ordinary watchman, placing Hadjar under the scrutiny of the officer who handles the ship's practical discipline.
characters.name: Bosun of Rook's Wings

characters.description: A peak heaven-soldier pirate sent onto Rook's Wings during the border attack. She knows Hadjar's identity and states that an unnamed client has paid to have him taken alive, turning the assault on the warship into a targeted abduction attempt.
characters.name: Pirate retrieval agent

recaps.ending: Einen survives Tom's attack and receives further healing arranged by Dora, leaving him alive but separated from Hadjar for the border mission. Tom also survives after Hadjar breaches the sanctioned duel and cuts through his imperial armor. Hadjar accepts an elder lord as a prospective mentor, but must gain inner-circle status before receiving his sword-spirit instruction. He also owes Dora for Einen's care and remains bound to the seven-year deadline imposed by the elf healer: he must reach lord level before the protective poison becomes fatal. The ancient enemy's soul fragment, the raven ancestor, rival inheritors, Helmer's Tournament of Twelve obligation, and the Raven sect remain unresolved. Hadjar departs alone to retrieve a Wastelands scroll from Fort Derrigan, but an unknown client hires pirates to capture him alive. After Rook's Wings is attacked, Hadjar kills the pirate sent for him and escapes on her flying mount. The mount crashes beyond the border, breaking Hadjar's bones. Rook's Wings also falls, and the fates of its commander and crew are unknown. Hadjar ends the book stranded in hostile territory while war with Laskin approaches.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar and Einen enter the Holy Sky School at its lowest rank, survive extortion, house vendettas, a disastrous giant hunt, and war with rival disciples, then earn promotion to full disciples. Dora becomes their ally and fulfills her promise to replace Hadjar's spatial ring. A massacre in the capital reveals that rival descendants of the Black General hunt one another. Elven leaders discover a large fragment of that ancient enemy's soul sealed inside Hadjar, and a healer gives him seven years to reach lord level before her conditional poison kills him. Tom later defeats and nearly kills Einen in a sanctioned duel. Hadjar breaks into the arena, wounds Tom, and attracts an elder sword mentor, who sends him toward Fort Derrigan for an ancient scroll. Pirates attack his transport on behalf of an unknown client who wants him alive. Hadjar kills the retrieval agent but crashes beyond the western border, injured and alone in hostile territory.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar survived Underworld City and became a heaven soldier, carrying a dangerous inherited sword power and the legacy of his dragon mentor, Traves. Einen remained his closest companion. Rahaim gave the pair recommendations to the Holy Sky School, offering them a route into the far more powerful cultivation world of the Empire. They begin this volume intending to use those recommendations to seek admission and advancement together.

Two months after their meeting with Rahaim, Hadjar and Einen leave Underworld City. Shock chooses another path, carrying Ilmena's ribbon and intending to report the dead to their families. The friends cross the Empire with a noble caravan and then aboard a flying frigate, arriving in the capital with little money and only two examination days remaining. At the Holy Sky School they find an extraordinary field of young heaven soldiers and deliberately apply at the lowest, ordinary-disciple rank. A hostile heir of the Predatory Blades clan takes offense at Hadjar, creating an early enemy. Dalit's crushing pressure eliminates almost every ordinary applicant, but both companions endure it and pass the age test. In the final trial, Einen drives his staff spear deep into a steel monolith. Hadjar summons his black blade and cuts the monolith in half. Mentor Jean admits them both as ordinary disciples. Their entry succeeds, but examiner Markin has secretly recognized Hadjar and begun coveting his name for an alchemical pill.

School life immediately exposes the cost of low status. Ordinary disciples receive no teaching, pay inflated prices, and must earn glory points before seeking promotion. Hadjar and Einen build a defended hut in the Forest of Knowledge and refuse an established disciple's demand for their starting points. Meanwhile, the Predatory Blades heir orders his sword-wielding attendant to punish them. She overwhelms and injures Hadjar but holds back before the final blow. Hadjar develops a powerful attachment to her and resolves to overcome the gulf between them. During a gathering task in the Forest of Shadows, more than thirty extortionists ambush the pair. Hadjar removes the archers while Einen holds the melee fighters with his armored ape manifestation. Fighting back-to-back, they kill the attackers despite exhaustion and dwindling medicine. Their leader then opens a supposedly formal duel with a surprise artifact attack, but Einen kills him with the River Serpent technique. As the wounded friends gather the spoils, Dora, a formidable elf carrying an imperial hammer, intercepts them and offers knowledge about her people.

Dora needs Hadjar's spatial ring for a forbidden elven technique. After threats fail, she offers compensation and swears a mutual non-harm oath, so Hadjar and Einen agree to help. She explains the origin of elves and leads them through hostile spirits that repeatedly identify Hadjar as a descendant of an ancient enemy. At the Forest of Shadows spirit's domain, Dora uses the ring to steal part of the spirit's power for her house and her Tournament of Twelve ambitions. Hadjar takes primordial water as payment, and Dora promises a much better ring within six months. On returning, the companions learn that the dead extortionist served House Tarez, whose agents now seek revenge. Hadjar uses most of the primordial water to widen and lengthen his meridians, making his techniques faster and stronger through a dangerous process his mixed human and dragon nature barely permits. Unconscious afterward, he meets Traves within his inner realm. A memory of Traves's old sword master teaches Hadjar about the Sword's Heart and a personal Kingdom of the Sword. Traves then reveals that Hadjar is his distant descendant through the Duran bloodline and carries a future obligation to him.

Hadjar renews his purpose and completes Azure Cloud, the seventh stance of Light Breeze. He and Einen travel to the Valley of Swamps for a gathering task, where Dora recruits them into a large hunt led by the Predatory Blades heir. Before the expedition begins, House Tarez servant Ian Gore confronts them. The hunt's contract prevents his full group from joining in, so Hadjar kills Ian's two allies and fights him alone. Ian uses restricted lightning techniques and repeated enhancements that poison his own body. Hadjar survives the escalation, kills him, claims his glory points, and secretly finds a red demonic stone among his possessions. Hadjar later meets Helmer, the Lord of Nightmares, inside Einen's shadow barrier. In exchange for the stone, Helmer claims that the Black General was an ancient spirit and Hadjar's ancestor, known to demons as Darkhan. He also admits supplying Ian with the stone, prohibited techniques, and training. The information comes at a cost: Hadjar is obligated to enter the Tournament of Twelve once he can qualify, which first requires reaching the school's inner circle.

Helmer's hint teaches Hadjar that the Black Blade can consume energy stones. The giant hunt then reveals a more dangerous test. Around fifteen hundred cultivators confront an intelligent primeval giant while the Predatory Blades heir secretly prepares a formation that treats most participants as expendable bait. The giant's stomps, stone attacks, and regenerating golems kill large numbers as Hadjar, Einen, Dora, and the elite heirs climb toward a scar on its neck. A Phoenix Crypt spell burns and shrinks the giant but also devastates nearby disciples and the formation users. During the final assault, Hadjar drives the Black Blade into the scar and secretly drains concentrated spirit essence from the giant's artery. The hunt leader's indiscriminate artifact strike wounds Hadjar, but the artery is severed and the giant dies. Einen saves Hadjar from the collapsing body. When the extracted core proves much weaker than expected, the heir suspects Hadjar and attacks him. Dora blocks the killing blow and openly condemns the sacrifice of fellow disciples. Only about two hundred and fifty hunters survive, and Hadjar has gained both valuable giant blood and the lasting hostility of the hunt's leader.

The dispute over the giant ends with Hadjar receiving extra compensation. He and Einen determine that the Black Blade absorbed roughly a quarter of the giant's power and has advanced into a heaven-level artifact. They swear secrecy strong enough to resist mental interrogation. Beneath the giant's corpse, a summons in the wind leads Hadjar to an underground river containing dreamgrass.
