He resists its attacks on his memories, harvests a large supply, and shares it with Einen after using some for his own cultivation. On the Imperial Road, roughly three thousand cultivators from two rival schools block the surviving Holy Sky School force. Despite being outnumbered more than ten to one, the smaller group attacks. Hadjar initially falters after killing a very young opponent, but Einen returns him to the battle. In the crisis, Hadjar grasps the Sword's Heart and recognizes freedom as the principle behind his swordsmanship. He defeats a powerful opponent and survives an honorable duel with a better-equipped full disciple, who withdraws with a promise of a rematch. Griffin riders from Dora's house drive off the rival force. Only sixty-three Holy Sky School cultivators survive the road battle.

Back at school, the companions convert their battlefield gains into enough glory points for the promotion exam. Einen reveals that he secretly practices unlicensed alchemy, having hidden it to protect Hadjar from the consequences. A mysterious long-lived mentor takes an interest in Hadjar, while the Treasure Tower keeper sells both friends their examination scrolls. They turn the public test into a betting event, with Dora wagering on a rapid success. In the first stage, Hadjar withstands an artifact's weapon pressure, deepens his sword insight, and destroys its escalating lightning technique without drawing his physical sword. He then eliminates five peak heaven-soldier golems with a single black crescent and becomes a full disciple. Einen's test forces him to define the purpose of his weapon. Remembering the weapon his father gave him and the escape his father enabled, he realizes that his path is protection and manifests a defensive weapon-in-the-heart technique. He also passes the golem trial. Both friends receive gold tokens and full-disciple status. After collecting their winnings, Dora uses her authority to take them into the capital and fulfill her promise to replace Hadjar's spatial ring.

A master artifact maker gives Hadjar a bound heaven-level ring with a large storage space. Dora then takes the companions to an elite restaurant, where Hadjar turns a former battlefield opponent into a respectful prospective rival. Assassins storm the building and target Dora with poisoned bolts. Einen shields her and is gravely wounded. Hadjar and the young noble swordsman fight together, but the noble takes a poisoned bolt meant for Hadjar. The group escapes into a sealed garden, where a female spirit-knight assassin offers an antidote only if Hadjar defeats her. She reveals that she shares the Black General's inheritance and has killed many other inheritors to take their power. Hadjar pierces her with the Black Blade and drains her spirit, but she summons a blood spirit and reaches power comparable to a lord. Using a golden elixir and the inherited image of the Black General, Hadjar breaks the garden veil and kills her. Her last poisoned dagger strikes the noble swordsman, who dies after acknowledging Hadjar as a friend. Dora's elder sister carries the survivors away for treatment. Unconscious, Hadjar meets a talking raven that claims authority over him by descent.

An elf healer cures Einen and improves his damaged energy body, but Hadjar's condition is more dangerous. She finds a severe wound in his soul and an ancient dark force that repels her examination. Within himself, Hadjar confronts the raven-form ancient enemy, who offers to become his master and teach him unmatched swordsmanship in return for cooperation against the gods. Hadjar refuses, remaining loyal to Traves. The elf ruler regards him as a danger and prepares to execute him, but the elves' ancestral tree intervenes. The healer and ruler explain that the ancient enemy's soul was divided after the Great War and scattered through bloodlines. Hadjar carries one of fewer than ten large fragments, sealed inside part of his own soul. The fragment has grown by consuming another, and the seal may eventually allow the enemy to possess him. His inherited Black Blade is a separate spirit weapon. The healer administers a seven-colored poison that reinforces the seal and buys time. Hadjar must reach lord level within seven years, in which case the poison disappears. If he fails, it kills him in the eighth year.

Hadjar finds Einen fully recovered, and the elf ruler ultimately releases both men as guests while departing for an imperial war council. Panic spreads through the capital amid fear of war with Laskin. Back at school, Tom challenges Einen to a sanctioned dawn duel. The Treasure Tower offers no suitable new technique, but the healer's work has greatly strengthened Einen's channels and defensive manifestation. Under a lord's binding barrier, Einen withstands Tom's opening attack and hurls him into the arena wall with River Serpent. Tom recovers behind his imperial equipment, overwhelms Einen with superior speed and the Thunder God Sword, and uses the wounded man to pressure Dora into accepting a proposal. When she refuses to answer, Tom drives his sword into Einen's chest. Hadjar attacks the supposedly lord-proof barrier in a rage, combining his call and Black Blade strongly enough to crack it. He breaks into the arena, seizes Tom, and cuts him. Although Einen's survival remains uncertain at this point, Hadjar has violated a formal duel and placed himself directly against an inner-circle heir under the eyes of the school's lords.

Hadjar discovers that Einen is alive and moves him outside the damaged arena, then continues fighting Tom despite being outmatched. Tom's lightning defenses and proprietary high-speed techniques repeatedly wound him. Hadjar answers with Black Wind, derived from the inherited image of an ancient sword strike, but cannot sustain the exchange. At the edge of defeat, a memory of Traves reveals the price attached to the dragon heart: Hadjar must kill the Dragon Emperor and plant a tree in the lost Dark Storm homeland. Hadjar then confronts the inner sword-spirit seal, breaks one of its lines, and returns with renewed blue-and-black power. Though Tom's blade passes through his side, Hadjar wounds him through imperial armor before collapsing. A school lord intervenes and claims Hadjar as a future disciple. Further memories show Traves restoring his destroyed homeland, losing his wife and unborn daughter to murder, attacking the Dragon Emperor, and being defeated and imprisoned. The Emperor denied ordering the murders, leaving responsibility unresolved. On waking, Hadjar accepts the lord as a prospective mentor, contingent on earning inner-circle status. Tom's sister also voices suspicion that Hadjar is the wanted Mad General, but he gives no answer.

Dora confirms that Einen survived and is receiving treatment, though he will need about two more weeks to recover. Hadjar promises to repay her for arranging that care. His prospective mentor offers a mission to retrieve an ancient Wastelands scroll from a friend at Fort Derrigan, with a large glory-point reward that would advance Hadjar toward the inner-circle examination. Fully healed by a pill included with the instructions, Hadjar accepts and joins the warship Rook's Wings as a watchman. Near the contested western border, the wind falls silent and an ambush begins. Crossbow fire wounds the bosun and kills the coxswain before a heavily armed pirate ship closes in. Hadjar destroys incoming cannonballs, but a peak heaven-soldier pirate reveals that an unnamed client has paid to capture him alive. Hadjar leaps between the colliding ships, kills the retrieval agent, and commandeers her winged mount. The creature goes out of control and crashes, breaking Hadjar's bones. Rook's Wings also falls. Hadjar survives, injured and separated from every ally, but realizes that the crash has stranded him beyond the border in hostile imperial territory.

characters.description: A dragon-blooded sword cultivator and former soldier who begins this volume unconscious and critically wounded. His ancient tigress companion carries him out of the borderland forest toward the travelers who may save him.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.description: Hadjar's devoted ancient-beast protector. She changes from a white cub into a powerful tigress, carries the gravely injured Hadjar away from forest predators, and brings him within reach of three passing cultivators.
characters.name: Hadjar's ancient tigress companion

characters.description: The local baron's son and a Red Mule School inner-circle disciple traveling with Aaliyah and Irma. He is among the three cultivators who encounter a tigress carrying a gravely wounded stranger in the borderland forest.
characters.name: Derek

characters.description: A Red Mule School inner-circle disciple traveling with Derek and Irma. She is among the three cultivators who encounter Hadjar and his tigress in the borderland forest, and she supports the decision to help the gravely wounded stranger.
characters.name: Aaliyah

characters.description: A Red Mule School inner-circle disciple and one of the travelers who find Hadjar near the border. She accompanies Derek and Aaliyah as they decide how to help the injured stranger despite the danger and uncertainty surrounding him.
characters.name: Irma

characters.description: A spirit-knight healer at the border military hospital. With precise control of energy needles, the healer undertakes the difficult repair of Hadjar's unusually damaged channels and preserves his cultivation foundation.
characters.name: Border healer

characters.description: The leader of the vast orc alliance that arrives outside the border fort. He halts the army and demands talks rather than beginning an attack.
characters.name: Orc chief

characters.description: The senior officer directing the border fort's defenses and evacuation preparations. She plans to destroy its stores rather than let the approaching orc force capture them.
characters.name: Border fort commander

characters.description: An ancient demon with an unexplained interest in Hadjar. Invisible to everyone except Hadjar and the tigress, he kills a hidden spy during the orc negotiations.
characters.name: Helmer

characters.description: An elite tattooed axe fighter selected to test Hadjar and accompany him against the demons. His acceptance must be earned under the customs of the orc hunters before the campaign can begin.
characters.name: Orc hunter

characters.description: A spiritual leader who appears through four age-aspects associated with curiosity, wisdom, pride, and freedom. He challenges Hadjar's ideas about identity and draws him into an unexplained vision during the hunter rite.
characters.name: Orc shaman

characters.description: The orc hunter's half-human, half-orc wife and a personal link across the border between the two peoples. Her husband leaves her with the tribes when he departs alongside Hadjar on the campaign into occupied territory.
characters.name: Orc hunter's wife

characters.description: A cloaked Raven Sect cultivator accompanied by a raven. His arrival at the border tavern provokes an immediate, hungry reaction from Hadjar's Black Blade.
characters.name: Raven Sect cultivator

characters.description: A female-presenting enemy who confronts Hadjar's party at the recently destroyed border fort.
characters.name: Ruined-fort demon

characters.description: An ancestral enemy fragment already bound within Hadjar before this volume begins. It remains a threat within his soul.
characters.name: Black General

characters.description: A lord-level Border Legion officer who arrives with soldiers after Hadjar's duel with the Raven Sect envoy. He recognizes the unusual quality of Hadjar's sword attack, secures the scene, and begins investigating the combatants.
characters.name: Border Legion officer

characters.description: A powerful representative of the gods who appears after Hadjar completes the waterfall ordeal. She approves action against demons that have violated divine law, but warns Hadjar that his own conduct is now under scrutiny.
characters.name: Divine fairy messenger

characters.description: A blue-eyed, half-human operative serving the demon prince near the enslaved fields. She is a powerful border agent, and Hadjar chooses to capture her as a possible source of intelligence.
characters.name: Half-human demon woman

characters.description: The half-human border operative captured and bound by Hadjar. While she leads him out of the gorge, he recognizes her as the demon king's daughter.
characters.name: Demon king's daughter

characters.description: The ruler behind the demon forces occupying the borderlands. His planned expansion seeks to establish a demon empire recognized by the laws of heaven and earth.
characters.name: Demon king

characters.description: The demon king's expansionist son and a commander near the enslaved fields. Hadjar overhears him discussing the capture of a human fort, a missing operative, and the creation of an empire before ambushing one of his attendants.
characters.name: Demon prince

characters.description: The demon kingdom's co-ruler and an initial nameless-stage cultivator. The captive guide identifies her as a power equal in stage to the king, placing both rulers far beyond the direct fighting strength of Hadjar's party.
characters.name: Demon queen

characters.description: A Raven Sect swordsman who returns to challenge Hadjar at the Drunken Goose Tavern.
characters.name: Raven Sect challenger

characters.description: A mid-stage spirit-knight commanding the pirate ship that attacks Hadjar's cargo brig. He leads the final attempt to stop Hadjar's journey while the urgent sealed dispatch remains in the cultivator's sole custody.
characters.name: Pirate captain

recaps.ending:
The Black Star ritual ends when Hadjar kills Irma, preventing the altered child within her from founding the king's lawful demon empire. The wounded king is trapped in a revelation-ore cell, but his death is not confirmed, and the queen's fate is also unknown. Helmer rescues Hadjar, Derek, and the orc hunter from the collapsing gorge and reveals that the prophecy and expedition served his plan to extract the half-human demon woman. She survives, but her destination and Helmer's larger purpose remain unclear.

Derek survives scarred and missing an eye. Grieving Aaliyah and Irma, he takes a blood oath to kill Hadjar and leaves alone. The orc hunter returns alive to his pregnant wife, though he has lost an arm, part of a leg, and an eye. Hadjar learns that only three of his weapon-essence seal's 999 lines are broken, while the caged first Darkhan fragment claims it can seize him in six years and eleven months unless he reaches lordhood. After advancing and settling a Raven Sect challenge, Hadjar reports to the border fort, refuses to betray the tribes, and accepts an urgent dispatch. He destroys a pirate attack and continues toward the capital as sole courier, with the seal calculation underway.
recaps.in_short: After surviving a fall near a contested border, Hadjar repays the three school disciples who save him by joining an orc campaign against a demon kingdom. An orc hunter becomes his partner and spiritual teacher, helping him awaken his blue-bird spirit and begin resisting the seal on his sword path. The party infiltrates the demon palace with the king's half-human daughter, but Aaliyah dies and Irma is taken for a ritual intended to legitimize a demon empire. Hadjar kills Irma to stop it, and the survivors trap the wounded king in revelation ore. Helmer then admits that he arranged the expedition to extract the half-human daughter. Derek loses an eye, blames Hadjar for both women's deaths, and swears to kill him. Hadjar returns the maimed hunter to his tribe, advances his cultivation, and resumes his military obligation. He ends the volume traveling alone toward the capital with an urgent sealed scroll while his neural network calculates how to dismantle the remaining 996 lines of his weapon-essence seal.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar Darkhan is a dragon-blooded sword cultivator and former soldier whose path has carried him through repeated conflicts. He travels with a devoted ancient tigress and bears the Black Blade. A hostile fragment connected to the first Darkhan is bound within him, leaving an ancestral danger intertwined with his own cultivation.

Hadjar survives a disastrous fall into a borderland forest, but his body and energy channels are critically damaged. His ancient tigress brings him to Derek, Aaliyah, and Irma, three Red Mule School disciples who stabilize him and carry him to a military fort. A specialist healer saves his cultivation foundation, though he remains weakened.

An enormous orc alliance then approaches the fort. Hadjar's military experience convinces him that the force is fleeing rather than preparing a conventional siege. The orc chief asks for him by name and explains that demons are consuming the tribes, turning the defeated into obedient servants, and threatening humans as well. Helmer, the Lord of Nightmares, appears unseen during the talks and pushes Hadjar toward the same enemy for reasons of his own.

The orcs believe a prophecy requires Hadjar and one of their hunters to strike the demons' leader. Hadjar accepts because he owes his rescuers, wants to protect the fort, and needs a rare fern held by the tribes. Before the campaign can begin, he must prove himself against an elite orc axe fighter.

The orc preparation repairs Hadjar enough to face the hunter. Though outmatched in direct combat, he turns the formal duel into a double ring-out. The hunter condemns the tactic, but Hadjar argues that survival matters more than ritual honor when an entire people is threatened. The chief accepts this reasoning and assigns the reluctant hunter as Hadjar's partner. Helmer separately demands that Hadjar recover an unspecified object from the demon ruler.

Before departure, the orc shaman draws Hadjar into a personal trial. Hadjar experiences another life as a disabled musician restored by a neural implant. Three years of wealth and excess leave that man without purpose until an armed attack forces him to choose whether to protect strangers at the cost of his own life. In the decisive moment, he rejects surrender and acts to save a mother and child.

The trial identifies the musician as Hadjar Darkhan and reconnects his survival with a chosen purpose. Hadjar wakes in the orc camp with his name tattoo expanded across his arm, carrying memories whose exact reality remains uncertain.

The shaman recognizes Hadjar's ordeal as a personal trial and the orcs honor him with an earned name. Derek, Aaliyah, and Irma insist on joining the expedition, while the orc hunter leaves his half-human, half-orc wife behind. The group crosses the border using a prisoner disguise and stops at a tavern for supplies.

A Raven Sect envoy offers Hadjar membership, claiming that Hadjar and the sect share a fragment of the same ancestor. Hadjar refuses because he has already given his word elsewhere. Their dispute becomes a duel against a stronger spirit knight. Pressed toward defeat, Hadjar abandons reliance on borrowed power and discovers a sword expression of his own, turning the surrounding rain into blades. A Border Legion force interrupts the fight, allowing the wounded envoy to escape. Its lord-level officer releases Hadjar only after binding him by oath to report to a military fort when his present task is done.

The orc hunter now recognizes Hadjar as a fellow hunter and begins teaching him the ancestral path. His lessons place spirit before body and weapon, offering Hadjar a possible route toward understanding both his own power and the hostile inheritance within him.

Hadjar's party enters occupied territory and finds settlements stripped of life. At a ruined fort, a demon enthralls Derek, Aaliyah, and Irma through mental compulsion. The tigress frees Hadjar from the attack, leaving him and the orc hunter to manage the threat. Hadjar kills the demon with the Black Blade, and the hunter admits that he allowed the confrontation to test whether Hadjar could resist temptation. The companions recover and refuse to retreat.

Scouting reveals the true scale of the enemy: thousands of demons at spirit-knight strength or above, backed by innumerable transformed servants. A direct assault is impossible. The hunter carries an ancient fang intended to kill the demon king, but the weapon still has to be brought within reach of him. Hadjar proposes avoiding the army entirely by flying over it. The campaign therefore changes from an open advance into an infiltration. The group begins searching the old wreck sites for a sky vessel that can be restored and used to reach the demon stronghold.

The party recovers a crashed military schooner and begins repairing it. During the work, Derek explains that his hostility toward the opposing empire comes from his mother's death after enemy scouts captured her. Hadjar and Derek deepen their friendship even while acknowledging that imperial loyalties may someday divide them.

The orc hunter delays the mission long enough to train Hadjar's spirit. A grave-grown root carries Hadjar into a spirit realm where a Guardian, an earth being, and a titanic dragon direct and test him. The dragon recognizes his lineage and sends him toward the Tree of Souls. There Hadjar learns that the spirit world is also a reflection within his soul.

The black general within him claims kinship and tries to consume him, but Hadjar rejects that hostile fragment. His true spirit appears as a sleeping blue bird. By accepting it, Hadjar returns to his body able to manifest the bird despite not yet being a spirit knight. He has opened the ancestral path and separated his own nature from the enemy presence inside him.

The orc hunter takes Hadjar through body training while the others finish the schooner. He also reveals that his pregnant wife is waiting with the tribes. Hadjar offers to carry the king-killing weapon alone, but the hunter refuses to abandon the campaign.

Hadjar drinks a powerful wolf-broth preparation and must climb a lethal waterfall to retain its benefits. Cutting water, hidden rocks, storm winds, and red lightning drive his channels and nodes to reinforce his body directly. He reaches the summit and gains another mark in his name tattoo. A divine messenger then appears, saying the gods approve of destroying the lower demons because they have broken a magistrate's law. Her approval comes with a warning: she will watch Hadjar and destroy both him and the fragment in his soul if he violates that law himself.

The hunter tests Hadjar's strengthened body and accepts him as a free hunter in spirit. The two agree to a future rematch. They return to Derek, Aaliyah, Irma, and the tigress, who have made the repaired vessel ready for flight.

The repaired schooner becomes the Drunken Goose and carries the party over demon territory. Its route crosses a storm vortex guarded by hundreds of winged serpentine beasts. Hadjar wants their cores for his cultivation, but the swarm quickly proves too large for a clean passage. The crew uses cannon fire and an ignited ash mixture to burn the pursuing beasts while Hadjar turns the vortex itself into an escape route.

The maneuver succeeds only at great cost. Hadjar destroys part of the vortex, loses the strongest core he was pursuing, and watches the damaged vessel fall into the rocks. The tigress saves the group during the crash but is badly injured and must sleep for about a week. The orc hunter treats the other survivors, restoring them enough to continue.

The Drunken Goose is beyond recovery, leaving the party stranded in a hostile gorge. Hadjar scouts ahead and discovers signs of enslaved inhabitants rather than an ordinary military camp. The human companions also cannot withstand the region's atmosphere without protection, so the group must find another route into the enemy center.

Hadjar discovers fields filled with enslaved dead and overhears the demon prince discussing conquest. He captures a powerful half-human demon woman who proves to be the king's daughter. Bound by a carefully framed oath, she reports that the kingdom contains thousands of demons and that both king and queen stand at the nameless stage. She becomes the party's unwilling guide.

The guide explains that the king plans to use the Black Star night to conceive a half-human child within the world's laws, allowing him to establish a lawful demon empire. With only two days left, Hadjar's companions disguise themselves as captives and enter the palace under her authority. They pass its spiritual defenses, assume servant disguises, and approach the feast.

Hadjar and the orc hunter launch their assassination attempt, but the king has prepared a substitute artifact and is overwhelmingly stronger. He recognizes Hadjar's ancestral connection, defeats the attackers, and kills Aaliyah. Irma is taken as the intended bride for the ritual. Hadjar, Derek, and the hunter are sent toward the slave fields, leaving the first assault a complete failure.

Hadjar, Derek, and the orc hunter wake in energy-suppressing cells. Derek grieves Aaliyah, who was his intended wife, and blames Hadjar's failed plan. Hadjar nevertheless uses residual power in an altered finger to access his spatial ring and remove the bars. The three choose to keep fighting rather than escape while Irma remains in the king's hands.

They capture the half-human guide again and learn that her apparent betrayal resulted from the split between her human oath and demon nature. Outside the palace veil, the oath governed her actions. Inside, her demon side could obey the king. Even so, she preserved Hadjar's ring, arranged survivable cells, and kept the genuine king-killing dagger hidden. She also reveals that the king raped her mother and that she has spent years seeking revenge against him and the queen.

The guide has mapped a secret route from the cells to the ritual site. Nearby revelation ore can suppress even the rulers' power, and the king should be vulnerable during the ritual. The survivors now have about a day and a half to prepare a second assault.

Before the final assault, Hadjar confronts the first Darkhan fragment within his soul and cages it. The fragment claims it will seize his body in six years and eleven months unless he reaches lordhood. With revelation ore weakening the mark on his sword path, Hadjar begins cutting its lines despite damage to his own soul.

The group reaches the ritual as the king uses Irma to create the intended child. The half-human daughter holds off the queen while Hadjar, Derek, and the orc hunter fight through the guards with revelation-ore weapons. All three are badly injured, and the hunter is mutilated by a lord-level defender. Hadjar finally reaches the ritual cocoon and kills Irma, ending the altered life in her womb and disrupting the Black Star plan.

The king transforms and pursues Hadjar through the palace. Following a prepared route, Hadjar damages the king's neck and a major meridian with the Black Blade. The orc hunter then seals the wounded ruler inside a revelation-ore cell, where suppression is expected to kill him within minutes. The palace begins collapsing around them before that death is confirmed.

Hadjar wakes outside the destroyed gorge with Derek and the maimed orc hunter. Winged serpents consume the remaining demons and undead, while revelation ore and ash are expected to confine the beasts for thousands of years. Helmer claims responsibility for saving the three survivors.

Hadjar realizes that Helmer fabricated the prophecy and steered the expedition toward this outcome. The Lord of Nightmares wanted the half-human demon woman removed from the kingdom and enabled her extraction after her battle with the queen. Helmer confirms that she survived, but does not explain her destination or his full purpose. Hadjar's prior obligations involving House Tarez and the Tournament of the Twelve remain in force.

Derek survives with severe facial scars and one eye lost. The orc hunter has lost an arm, part of one leg, and an eye. Grief over Aaliyah and Irma drives Derek to attack Hadjar. Hadjar hides Helmer's role and accepts the blame. Derek swears a blood oath to kill him and departs alone. Hadjar then carries the injured hunter back toward the orc tribes.

Hadjar returns the orc hunter to his wife and tribe. The hunter survives the campaign permanently maimed, while his pregnant wife receives him home. The tribal chief invites Hadjar to the victory celebration and directs him to consult the shaman before resuming his overdue military obligation.

The shaman identifies Hadjar's mark as a weapon-essence seal made of 999 lines. Despite Hadjar's efforts during the palace campaign, only three lines have been broken, leaving 996 still obstructing his true path. The shaman cannot grant him freedom and insists that Hadjar must reclaim it through his own effort. He does provide ancient fern-root powder, the resource Hadjar originally hoped to obtain by helping the tribes.

Hadjar uses the powder in dragon meditation, drawing its energy through his heart and into his core. The process advances his cultivation to the advanced stage. Strengthened but still burdened by the seal and the imprisoned soul-fragment, he finally leaves the tribes and sets out for the border fort where his oath requires him to report.

On the road to the fort, Hadjar is challenged by a returning Raven Sect swordsman. He survives the spirit knight's attack, kills the challenger with his sixth stance, and takes the fallen man's spatial chain. A mortal farmer then gives him a cart ride and a straw hat, receiving one hundred imperial coins in return.

At the fort, Hadjar's appearance initially leads a guard to mistake him for a vagrant. His weapon-heart aura brings the commander to the gate, where the seal on Hadjar's letter establishes his mission. The commander already knows that the orcs have left the region and held a victory festival, but Hadjar refuses to reveal the tribes' secret. Instead of detaining him, the officer entrusts him with an overdue and urgently sealed scroll for the capital. Hadjar departs as its sole courier aboard a cargo brig.

The pirate ship responsible for his earlier aerial disaster attacks the brig. Hadjar boards it alone, destroys the vessel, and kills its spirit-knight captain. He continues toward the capital with the scroll. At the same time, his neural network finishes reconfiguring and begins calculating how to destroy the remaining 996 lines of the weapon-essence seal.

characters.description: A Holy Sky School disciple and swordsman who returns after six weeks away. Though still an advanced Heaven Soldier, his body rivals that of a mid-stage Spirit Knight. His neural network now operates through his own mind, while a dangerous presence remains hidden within him.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.description: A school mentor pursuing the Hundred Voices pill and revenge against the Emperor. He confines a summoned glyph in an alchemical cauldron and secretly arranges for a returned subject to be delivered for name extraction after reaching Spirit Knight.
characters.name: Holy Sky School alchemist

characters.description: Hadjar's prospective master at the Holy Sky School. An unusually powerful swordsman, he warns Hadjar to trust no one, accepts a letter from him, grants him 80,000 glory points, and sends him to the seventh training arena.
characters.name: Hadjar's supervising swordsman

characters.description: Hadjar's trusted friend and fellow Holy Sky disciple. Recently promoted to the inner circle, he helped Dora and the Dinos siblings repel attackers at the school gates.
characters.name: Einen

characters.description: A Holy Sky disciple allied with Hadjar and Einen. She fought beside Einen and the Dinos siblings during the attack at the school gates.
characters.name: Dora

characters.description: The Holy Sky ally previously introduced as Dora is a mid-stage Spirit Knight and an heir of House Marnil. She joins Hadjar and Einen for the Wastelands expedition.
characters.name: Dora Marnil

characters.description: An advanced Spirit Knight and skilled swordswoman who accompanies Tom. She meets Hadjar again upon his return.
characters.name: Annis Dinos

characters.description: A peak Spirit Knight commanding the pirates who ambush Hadjar's group. She seeks revenge because Hadjar killed her daughters and refuses to identify the employer who hired her crew to seize him.
characters.name: Pirate captain

characters.description: An arrogant Spirit Knight swordsman whose awakened spirit is associated with thunderbolts. He has an unsettled rivalry with Einen, ending their first observed bout without a victory after Einen parries him.
characters.name: Tom Dinos

characters.description: Hadjar's ancient-beast companion, discovered alive after the earlier shipwreck. She survived by concealing herself in a small form.
characters.name: Hadjar's ancient tigress companion

characters.description: A hostile raven-like presence chained within a sarcophagus in Hadjar's soul-world. It calls Hadjar its descendant and addresses him directly, but its intentions are unclear.
characters.name: Hostile soul-fragment

characters.description: An ancient figure whom the hostile soul-fragment identifies as its disciple. He appears in the fragment's unverified account of the distant past.
characters.name: Erhard

characters.description: Erhard's uncle and the ruler of one of the Hundred Kingdoms. He leads a major army during the ancient war shown in the hostile fragment's account.
characters.name: King Eranos

characters.description: Erhard is identified in the hostile fragment's account as the Last King. The fragment claims that his enemies sealed him alive and that the supposed tomb of Emperor Decatur was built around his prison.
characters.name: Last King

characters.description: A powerful manipulator with an existing claim on Hadjar. He appears without warning, admits involvement in an earlier affair, and urges Hadjar to survive the danger ahead while withholding his reasons.
characters.name: Helmer

characters.description: A powerful court figure who learns that the Path Through the Clouds technique still exists. He kills the servant who delivered the evidence and postpones informing the Dragon Emperor while he searches for the practitioner so he can seize the technique first.
characters.name: Dragon official

characters.description: A lord-comparable spirit golem clad in ice armor. It attacks Hadjar's party inside Grevendor and withstands his Black Wind technique.
characters.name: Ice-armored spirit golem

characters.description: The apparent ruler of a hidden hall built entirely of ice. She compels Hadjar to answer questions about the Last King's inheritance while he is injured and under her control.
characters.name: Ice woman

characters.description: The former ice woman names her allegiance to the Winter Court. She dominates Hadjar's speech and movement with ease, then holds him within frozen bars that hinder his escape.
characters.name: Winter Court fae

characters.description: A peak Spirit Knight commanding six Dead Moon assassins under contracts against Hadjar and Einen. He offers to spare them only if they surrender their cultivation and Hadjar's ancient-beast core.
characters.name: Dead Moon Clan leader

characters.description: The mid-stage Spirit Knight leading the Eternal Mountain Clan expedition that holds the tomb key. He has unusually deep energy reserves and initially orders the captured Hadjar and Einen killed before hearing their offer of a copied map.
characters.name: Eternal Mountain Clan junior heir

characters.description: A hostile noble spearman traveling with the Eternal Mountain Clan expedition. He tries to attack Hadjar before Thea and her house's warriors stop him, and he resents both Hadjar and Thea.
characters.name: Eternal Mountain Clan spearman

characters.description: A mid-stage Spirit Knight who fights with a heavy sword and belongs to an impoverished great house. She stops a hostile spearman from attacking Hadjar and identifies herself as the sister of one of Hadjar's deceased former allies.
characters.name: Thea

characters.description: A nameless immortal encountered in an abandoned temple of the god of war. Although he calls himself a novice, his power lies beyond Hadjar's perception, and he already knows Hadjar's identity and history.
characters.name: Immortal servant of the god of war

characters.description: A maimed Red Mule School disciple and baron's son who once helped Hadjar. After the deaths of two expedition companions, he has sworn to kill Hadjar. A mysterious yellow light approaches him with an offer of power.
characters.name: Derek

characters.description: A bull-headed, golem-like keeper of the Last King's repository. It administers the third trial, requiring Hadjar to make it draw its sword within three attacks.
characters.name: Third-trial guardian

characters.description: The undead administrator of the repository's final trial and bearer of the divine artifact Wailing of Cities. Bound by the repository's rules, he immobilizes Hadjar and refuses to return him to the endangered Einen.
characters.name: Emperor Decatur

characters.description: An immensely powerful shadow that owns the graveyard of swords and offers Hadjar its personal inheritance. It identifies itself as Hadjar's ancestor and calls him uniquely worthy of the offer.
characters.name: Black General

characters.description: The Black General reveals that he is the First Darkhan and Hadjar's ancestor. A surviving fraction of a greater imprisoned being, he needs Hadjar alive because their fragments are attached and uses Dora's life to force acceptance of his inheritance.
characters.name: First Darkhan

characters.description: A giant cultivator who emerges alive from the repository disaster alongside Annis, the Dinos siblings, two archers, and the surviving tigress.
characters.name: Giant cultivator

characters.description: The snake-bodied leader of the demons that rebel against their governing laws. Helmer destroys her and presents her powerful core to Hadjar.
characters.name: Rebel demon commander

characters.description: A famed swordsman who arrives as three clan leaders press their claim against Hadjar. He declares Hadjar his disciple, deters the leaders, and takes him to Storm Mountain for two years of severe training.
characters.name: New swordsman master

recaps.ending: Hadjar passes the repository's trials, but the First Darkhan forces him to accept an inheritance by threatening Dora. The pact grants Hadjar Flying Sword while obliging him to keep studying the ancestor's knowledge, and the ancestor intends to use him as a vessel. Hadjar plans to turn that power against its owner. Dora remains alive after shielding Einen from Tom's attack, but her chest wound is fatal without rapid treatment. Einen, Annis, the Dinos siblings, the giant cultivator, and other allies escape aboard Dora's ship to seek her aunt's aid. Hadjar stays behind at the fort and spends nearly all his strength resisting the demon horde released by the repository's collapse. Helmer intervenes as the Demon Prince's emissary, erases the invading army, and gives Hadjar the rebel commander's core. Hadjar helps hide Helmer's role. The demon gates remain a wider threat, while Helmer's debts, the divine interest in Hadjar, the Dead Moon contract, Derek's oath, Dora's survival, and the First Darkhan's plan all remain unresolved. A famed swordsman finally claims Hadjar as his disciple and takes him to Storm Mountain for two years of dangerous training.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar returns to the Holy Sky School and joins Einen, Dora, Annis, and Tom in a search for Emperor Decatur's tomb. The expedition exposes imperial manipulation, a Winter Court fae, rival clans, assassins, and evidence that the tomb is actually the Last King's repository. Inside, Hadjar abandons revenge as his central purpose and adopts the identity North Wind. Dora is critically wounded saving Einen, while the First Darkhan coerces Hadjar into an inheritance pact that grants Flying Sword and prepares him as a future vessel. The repository's collapse reopens the demon gates. Einen and other allies carry Dora toward urgent treatment as Hadjar remains to defend the fort. Helmer destroys the invading horde for the Demon Prince and gives Hadjar its commander's core. Hadjar conceals this intervention, then leaves for two years of training on Storm Mountain with a new swordsman master.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar Darkhan survived war, loss, and repeated struggles against powers far above his cultivation. Known as the Mad General, he became a swordsman whose path is tied to an unusual neural network, the Black Blade, and a hostile presence lodged within his soul. His closest companion is Einen, a fellow warrior whose loyalty has endured danger and separation. Helmer, the Lord of Nightmares, has interfered in Hadjar's life and holds unresolved claims against him. Hadjar's earlier actions created enemies as well as allies, while the destruction of the Drunken Goose scattered members of a prior expedition and left lasting grievances.

Hadjar returns to the Holy Sky School as an advanced Heaven Soldier whose body is already comparable to a stronger cultivator. The school is preparing for imperial war games after a deadly attack, and Hadjar learns that Einen, Dora, and the Dinos siblings helped defend it. A map and key linked to Emperor Decatur's tomb have been recovered, giving Holy Sky disciples a short advantage in the coming search. Hadjar, Einen, and Dora leave for the Wastelands aboard Dora's flying ship, despite warnings that someone may be targeting Hadjar. A pirate frigate intercepts them. Einen boards the ship with Hadjar and sabotages its gunpowder hold, while Dora prevents the pirates from escaping. The captain admits that an unknown employer hired her crew to seize Hadjar, but her personal vendetta keeps her from naming that employer. Hadjar defeats her suicide attack, and he and Einen escape just before the frigate explodes. The immediate ambush ends, but the force behind the repeated attacks remains unidentified.

The travelers reach the fortress guarding entry to the Wastelands and reunite with Hadjar's ancient tigress, who survived the earlier shipwreck. Annis and Tom join the expedition, forming an alliance based on necessity rather than trust. Dora reveals that the original companions have faced repeated assassination attempts and traced the attackers' chain of command back to the Holy Sky School, though the person responsible remains unknown. Hadjar has memorized the tomb map, and Einen may be able to reproduce the key. After the group enters the Wastelands, Hadjar encounters the hostile raven-like fragment within his soul. The fragment calls him a descendant and presents an unverified history of Erhard, its disciple. In that account, Erhard was revived before birth, became a prodigious warrior, killed his uncle, united the Hundred Kingdoms, and became the Last King before his empire fell and his enemies sealed him alive. The fragment claims that the supposed tomb of Emperor Decatur was built around Erhard's prison and offers Hadjar a sword technique hidden there. Hadjar cannot tell whether the offer is guidance or a trap.

The expedition encounters dozens of blue-flamed guardians created as weapons in an ancient war. Ordinary attacks destroy only a few of them, and their fire wounds both physical and energy bodies. Annis reveals an extremely rare World River sword spirit, annihilating many guardians but collapsing from the damage it inflicts on her. When more enemies emerge, Hadjar refuses to abandon her. He joins willingly with his bird spirit through the ancestral path and releases an enhanced Black Wind that destroys the remaining formation. The effort stops his heart and leaves him near death, but the ancient tigress carries Hadjar and Einen away from the ruins. Hadjar eventually regains consciousness with grave physical injuries, while Annis begins recovering from severe damage to her energy channels. The group concludes that the map and key have recently awakened dormant defenses throughout the Wastelands. Their quest is no longer simply a race against rival cultivators - the artifacts themselves appear to be activating ancient dangers along the route.

The five travelers swear mutual secrecy over Annis's rare spirit and Hadjar's ancestral method, creating a fragile bond without removing their distrust. They learn that the history of the ancient war has been deliberately suppressed and that the seven empires answer to the Dragonlands. After avoiding a spirit-stage manticore, the group diverts toward red mountains. Annis tells Hadjar that her uncle murdered her parents and seized the Predatory Blades clan, leaving her and Tom alive in disgrace; revenge remains her driving purpose. Helmer then appears to Hadjar, admits manipulating an earlier affair, and warns him to survive an unexplained danger. In the mountains, Dora, Tom, and Annis disclose their hidden objective: Grevendor, an ancient site associated with the Last King's training. Their houses supplied artifacts and a secret map for this mission. A blizzard and confrontation force the nobles to share that map, but an enormous ice golem attacks before trust can be restored. Unable to defeat it, the party escapes by leaping into a ravine under Hadjar's protection and becomes trapped below.

The party follows the ravine to a concealed approach containing a flowering tree, a chasm, and a river of lethal celestial metal. Guided by information from the hostile fragment, Hadjar activates the entrance and reveals Grevendor beyond an invisible energy bridge. The bridge ends partway across, forcing Hadjar to continue on a rope while freezing pressure immobilizes his body and suppresses his sword power. He reaches the celestial-metal fumes and condenses enough material for the Path Through the Clouds technique. Elsewhere, a dragon official learns that this supposedly lost technique survives, kills the servant who brought the evidence, and decides to seize it before informing the Dragon Emperor. Hadjar then undertakes a dangerous advancement within his soul. Instead of following the technique exactly, he forges the celestial metal into protective dragon armor and incorporates his dragon call. Annis identifies him with the Mad General of legend while the others believe the process will kill him. Hadjar completes the transformation, advances to peak Heaven Soldier, and reaches the far side of the bridge. A powerful dragon pursuer is now searching for the unknown practitioner of his technique.

The remaining travelers cross the energy bridge and reach Grevendor's sealed gates. Hadjar's neural network identifies sword movements hidden in the gate reliefs, and Annis performs the paired form with him to open the way. Inside, the group follows the nobles' map through ancient corridors tied to the Last King. An ice-armored spirit golem attacks with strength comparable to a lord. Hadjar, Tom, Dora, Einen, and Annis combine their techniques, but the construct withstands their strongest blows and repeatedly regenerates. Annis takes command of a coordinated assault. Tom accepts severe backlash to create an opening, Hadjar forces the golem's guard down, and Dora, Annis, and Einen strike together. The golem responds with a freezing ray that incapacitates Dora and wounds the others. Tom uses a rare fire artifact to thaw her and damage the construct, but it begins restoring itself again. Seeing no conventional path to victory, Hadjar takes a stimulant and drives the golem over the complex's exterior edge. Both fall into the chasm, leaving his companions unable to determine whether he survived.

Hadjar awakens injured in a hidden ice hall ruled by a Winter Court fae. She controls his speech and movement, identifies his ancestry, and imprisons him in ice that suppresses his cultivation and artifacts. Helmer confirms that the fae is using Hadjar as bait. He offers an escape tool only if Hadjar accepts another unspecified future debt, and Hadjar agrees. The fae tries to make him submit by showing visions of his family and a possible death within a few years, but he refuses her offer of an eternal reunion. Einen, Dora, Annis, and Tom arrive before she can kill him. Using Helmer's staff splinter, Hadjar wounds the fae and takes the core she leaves behind. The victory exposes the nobles' concealed imperial mission: they came for the fae's core and expected Hadjar and Einen to emerge crippled or stripped of their abilities. Einen ends his personal friendship with Dora. Hadjar prevents the nobles from taking the core by force, then accepts Annis's claim through a sword-only duel. Although her formal technique initially outclasses him, he adapts, defeats her, and leaves Grevendor with Einen and the core.

Hadjar and Einen reunite with the ancient tigress and conclude that the wider plot may have placed Dora in danger as well as themselves. Helmer then takes both the fae core and the staff splinter under their existing agreement. He warns that a powerful family intends to kill Hadjar and keeps an eventual tournament obligation open. A week later, seven Dead Moon Clan assassins confront Hadjar and Einen under separate contracts, demanding their cultivation and an ancient-beast core. The leader's concealed movement technique overwhelms Hadjar, forcing him to let the neural network control his body temporarily. Its precise counterattacks kill one assassin and injure another, but Hadjar rejects permanent dependence on autonomous control even when the network predicts that taking command himself will be fatal. He merges his Quetzal spirit with the Black Blade and uses an enhanced Black Wind to kill two more attackers. The effort leaves him unconscious. The approach of many other cultivators forces the surviving assassins to withdraw, but their leader promises to return with a stronger clan technique. Hadjar and Einen survive, while the contracts against them remain active.

After disabling the neural network's compulsory control, Hadjar begins using its battle simulations for training. He and Einen continue toward the tomb and find the key's discovery site covered with hundreds of dead cultivators. Tracking the new key-holders leads them into the custody of an Eternal Mountain Clan expedition. Hadjar avoids execution by claiming that he and Einen can recreate the encrypted tomb map. Thea, the sister of a deceased former ally, protects him from a hostile spearman and later shares a brief intimacy with him, though neither treats it as a commitment. Hadjar redirects the expedition into an ancient underground route while planning to steal the key. He lures a stone crocodile into the party and secretly disrupts their attempt to kill it, causing several deaths. Thea repudiates him when he admits that he intended the monster to eliminate the expedition. With Hadjar and Einen exposed and ready to fight, the junior heir chooses negotiation. He apologizes and offers equality for as long as their goals coincide. The result is a conditional truce inside the ancient sewer route, with every faction expecting eventual betrayal.

Hadjar leads the uneasy alliance from the sewers into a ruined capital, where a mysterious light draws him to an abandoned temple of the god of war. An unnamed immortal servant explains that fairies belong to a wider system and says Hadjar's own path has been manipulated. He admits that he also wants to influence Hadjar and offers him the god of war's permanent mark, promising immense power. Hadjar refuses divine patronage and declares that he will reach the Seventh Heaven through his own efforts. Afterward, the same light approaches Derek, a maimed former companion who has sworn to kill Hadjar. At midday, the expedition follows a magical bird to the mound marked on Hadjar's map. Tom, Annis, and Dora ambush the Eternal Mountain group with a binding net, intending to seize both map and key. Hadjar and Einen use the confusion to bind the Dinos group in turn. They reveal that they retained the real artifacts all along, substituting copies while their rivals handled them. Leaving both competing groups trapped, Hadjar and Einen take the authentic map and key into the supposed tomb.

The mound proves to be a spatial artifact holding the Last King's repository rather than a conventional tomb. Blood activates the entrance, separating Hadjar and Einen inside a sequence of trials. Apparitions of Hadjar's dead family and friends accuse him of failure and urge him to betray Einen, but he recognizes them as false and rejects their conclusions. He decides that his purpose must extend beyond revenge toward freedom and protection for those subject to arbitrary power. After briefly reuniting, Hadjar and Einen are separated again by a shifting maze. Hadjar escapes by studying when its barriers appear, then faces a bull-headed guardian who demands that he make it draw its sword within three attacks. Raw strength and his most powerful technique fail. The guardian instead forces Hadjar to confront the fear and revenge governing his life. Hadjar accepts fear without submitting to it and commits himself to a new foundation. When he asks the guardian to draw, it does, confirming his success. Hadjar continues the battle, kills the guardian, and leaves the trial under the identity North Wind, dedicated to freedom rather than vengeance.

Hadjar reunites with Einen in a gravity-defying staircase maze where advancement requires defeating another challenger. They lure out an Eternal Mountain spearman and prepare explosives against the surrounding opportunists. Hadjar kills the spearman after their energy techniques disrupt the maze, but Tom attacks during the aftermath. Dora shields Einen and suffers a catastrophic chest wound. Before Hadjar can return to them, the repository pulls him into its final trial. The undead Emperor Decatur removes access to Hadjar's cultivation, soul, and sword powers, then offers safety if he abandons his path. Hadjar's concern for those he failed and for Einen leads him to reject an ordinary life. His will stops Decatur's descending sword, allowing him to pass. In a graveyard of immense swords, an ancient shadow offers its personal inheritance and reveals itself as the Black General. It explains that it is the First Darkhan, Hadjar's ancestor, and that its surviving self remains imprisoned elsewhere. When Hadjar resists, the ancestor threatens Dora's life. Hadjar accepts the inheritance under coercion while privately resolving to destroy the First Darkhan with the power it gives him.

The First Darkhan's inheritance binds Hadjar to study its knowledge and prepares him as a possible future vessel. It grants him Flying Sword, the first Sword of Four Strikes. The repository's collapse reopens the demon gates, and Hadjar returns to find many challengers dead and Dora alive but critically wounded. Einen carries her as the survivors flee to the fort. A healer says only Dora's aunt can save her, but the demon horde attacks before the group can depart normally. Hadjar holds the infirmary entrance, cuts Dora's ship free so Einen and the others can escape with her, and stays behind to defend the fort. He spends nearly all his strength using Flying Sword against the invaders. Helmer then arrives as an emissary of the Demon Prince. He explains that the rebel demons violated their own laws by seeking the world's destruction, erases the horde with nightmares, and gives Hadjar the commander's core. Hadjar helps conceal the intervention. When three clan leaders later press an unidentified claim against him, a famed swordsman declares Hadjar his disciple and deters them. Hadjar leaves for a potentially lethal two-year course of training on Storm Mountain, while Dora's survival and his ancestral pact remain unresolved.

characters.description: A powerful manipulator and creditor to whom Hadjar still owes unresolved obligations.
characters.name: Helmer

characters.description: A hostile ancestral fragment confined within Hadjar's soul. It seeks release through Hadjar, creating a struggle over identity and control.
characters.name: First Darkhan

characters.description: Hadjar's ancient-beast companion and protector, already known from his earlier travels. She is a formidable combatant and faithful ally.
characters.name: Primeval tigress

characters.description: A concealed tournament entrant who intervenes when a city guard is about to kill a street boy, pays the boy's gate fee, and hires him as a guide. His will alone can immobilize a spirit knight.
characters.name: Hooded swordsman

characters.description: An illegal courier who enters the capital with the hooded swordsman and serves as his guide.
characters.name: Street boy

characters.description: A celebrated war-games fighter credited with capturing and holding an enemy fort. Public reports also connect him closely with Dora Marnil.
characters.name: Einen

characters.description: A prominent young woman publicly associated with Einen. Reports from the capital describe their bond as romantic.
characters.name: Dora Marnil

characters.description: A renowned swordsman reported to have taken the black swordsman from the wasteland disaster to Storm Mountain as his disciple. Even before he appears directly, his reputation shapes the tournament's expectations.
characters.name: Orune

characters.description: The powerful head of Holy Sky School, entrusted with presiding over the tournament's power-stone test and explaining the standard by which thousands of entrants will be judged.
characters.name: Holy Sky School rector

characters.description: An elite swordswoman who once held the highest heir position in the Predatory Blades clan. Her younger brother Tom now outranks her formally, although her power exceeds the tournament test's normal scale.
characters.name: Annis Dinos

characters.description: Annis's younger brother and the current senior heir of the Predatory Blades clan. His elevation places him above his more visibly accomplished sister within the clan hierarchy.
characters.name: Tom Dinos

characters.description: A huge and exceptionally strong tournament entrant from the Eternal Mountain Clan. He produces an orange power-stone result without calling on his spirit.
characters.name: Eternal Mountain Clan giant heir

characters.description: The true black swordsman and Orune's disciple, revealed after defeating a convincing imitator in the tournament. He then reunites with his friend Einen.
characters.name: Hadjar Darkhan

characters.description: The leader of the Predatory Blades clan whom Annis and her allies intend to overthrow.
characters.name: Predatory Blades clan head

characters.description: The emperor and host of the Tournament of the Twelve. He shares an old, unusually familiar relationship with Orune and watches Hadjar's progress alongside the empire's leading powers.
characters.name: Morgan

characters.description: A Predatory Blades clan heir whose unexplained disappearance during the forest trial threatens Annis's plan, forcing Hadjar's squad to follow his trail and attempt a rescue.
characters.name: Predatory Blades heir

characters.description: A skeletal being with a demonic crystal heart that rules the hidden garden beneath the Lake of Dreams. It holds Hadjar's companions in enchanted sleep, claims to read fates, and draws Hadjar into an ancient memory.
characters.name: Crystal-hearted being

characters.description: The crystal-hearted jailer beneath the Lake of Dreams, now identified as an undead remnant of the ancient potter rather than the whole being. Ancient mages imprisoned it after drawing power from a godhood elixir, and it demands that Hadjar defeat it to free his sleeping companions.
characters.name: Lake of Dreams potter fragment

characters.description: Morgan's red-haired daughter, who draws Hadjar away from the reception and warns that conspirators intend to kill her father. She asks Hadjar to help prevent the assassination.
characters.name: Emperor's daughter

characters.description: A nameless-level swordsman identified in the princess's warning as one of four expected attackers during Morgan's reception speech.
characters.name: Nameless attacker

characters.description: An elven healer and Dora's aunt who treats Hadjar after the palace attack. Despite her medical care, she is openly distrustful of him because he descends from Darkhan.
characters.name: Dora's aunt

characters.description: A powerful dragon in human form who intercepts Hadjar outside the palace. His dragonlike eyes reveal his nature.
characters.name: Dragon-realm emissary

characters.description: An ancient and highly sophisticated golem that keeps the treasure tower. It knows Orune and recognizes how greatly Hadjar has changed.
characters.name: Treasure-tower keeper

characters.description: A member of the Dinos family paired against Hadjar in the tournament's fourth round. He enters as Hadjar's selected opponent while Hadjar is still grieving Orune's death.
characters.name: Dinos heir

recaps.ending: Orune uses an old law of masters and disciples to take responsibility for Hadjar's crimes, then kills himself with Morgan's sword. His sacrifice secures Hadjar's pardon, and Morgan orders a state funeral while retaining control of the empire. Hadjar enters the fourth tournament round immediately afterward and kills a Dinos heir with a newly manifested barony of the sword, leaving the Blue Wind Sword on the field. Einen, Dora, Annis, and the giant heir survive, while Annis's clan struggle and the giant heir's break with Eternal Mountain remain unresolved. Tom stood with them after Orune's death, but his later condition is not established. Hadjar is an initial-stage Spirit Knight with only a lead toward Path Through the Stars and about four years to overcome his divided-soul damage. The First Darkhan still seeks freedom through him, Helmer's obligations remain open, and a dragon emissary expects to revisit Hadjar's imperial lineage after the war. The book closes as Morgan orders general mobilization because Laskan has crossed the border.
recaps.in_short: Hadjar enters the Tournament of the Twelve after two years under Orune, joins Annis's conspiracy against her clan head, and destroys an undead potter fragment beneath the Lake of Dreams. A palace assassination attempt draws him into Morgan's ruthless preparations for war. Hadjar becomes a Spirit Knight, learns that he descends from a purged dragon imperial line, and refuses to support a dragon rebellion. He later gains a route toward Path Through the Stars, which may repair his divided soul. At an auction, Hadjar and Einen demand citizenship for neglected peoples in exchange for an ancient fae core, prompting Morgan to order their arrest. Orune assumes Hadjar's crimes and dies by Morgan's sword to absolve him. Grieving, Hadjar kills a Dinos heir in the tournament's fourth round and manifests barony of the sword. Morgan then announces mobilization as Laskan troops cross the border.

recaps.text: Previously: Hadjar Darkhan survived the destruction of his former royal life and became known as the Mad General and the black swordsman. His path joined him closely to Einen, Dora Marnil, and the ancient-beast tigress, while the hostile First Darkhan remained imprisoned within his divided soul. Helmer, the Lord of Nightmares, continued to hold obligations over him. Hadjar carried a dragon heart and the Black Blade, but poison damage left him with only a few years to reach lord level and prevent the collapse of his soul. Orune took Hadjar as his disciple and brought him to Storm Mountain for severe training. Meanwhile, Einen gained prominence in imperial war games and remained committed to Dora despite the political barriers to their marriage. War with Laskan drew nearer, and the Tournament of the Twelve offered Hadjar a place among the empire's strongest young cultivators.

The imperial capital is crowded for the Tournament of the Twelve as recruitment and artificial cultivation accelerate ahead of war with Laskan. A hooded swordsman saves a street boy from a fatal punishment, enters the city, and registers for the tournament. The prizes include rare artifacts and discipleship under a visiting master. Elite heirs quickly display strength beyond the first power-stone test, especially Annis Dinos, whose position in the Predatory Blades clan has passed to her younger brother Tom. A supposed black swordsman also enters, but the hooded competitor defeats him in the second round. The victor is then announced as Hadjar Darkhan, the true black swordsman and Orune's disciple. Hadjar reunites with Einen after two years apart and remains in the tournament.

Hadjar warns Einen that the Dead Moon Clan has used an imitator to pursue the core Einen conceals. He then meets Annis, Tom, Dora, and the giant heir, who plan to remove the head of the Predatory Blades clan before he can destroy them after the tournament. Hadjar joins primarily to support Einen, whose marriage to Dora depends on changing the balance of noble power. During the forest trial, their squad attacks Predatory Blades fighters but discovers that a missing clan relative has been dragged toward the Lake of Dreams. The lake's living fog defeats direct force and wounds the giant heir. Hadjar uses Flying Sword, an inherited technique that Orune did not teach him, to open a path through the barrier. His companions descend beneath the lake while he holds the spell back.

Beneath the Lake of Dreams, Hadjar's companions vanish into enchanted sleep while a skeletal being with a crystal heart confronts him. The being forces Hadjar to witness an ancient memory about a wanderer searching for his lost beloved, Tisse. It then identifies itself as an undead fragment of the legendary potter, imprisoned after ancient mages used a godhood elixir to power their island. The larger, soulless potter may still exist elsewhere. The fragment claims to know a forbidden truth and tells Hadjar that he is the key to escaping the garden. Hadjar instead fights alongside his Quetzal spirit and destroys the fragment's demonic heart. Mortally damaged, it warns him to distrust others and investigate the secret of his birth. Hadjar collapses after freeing the garden from its jailer.

Hadjar and the other survivors are recovered after the lake's destruction, but their dream wounds linger. Einen saw his dead mother, and two cultivators remain unable to wake. Hadjar and Einen place coercive leverage on a hostile Predatory Blades heir, deepening the risk of their planned coup. Helmer later confirms that he once gave the potter a heart and prevents Hadjar from voicing the fragment's feared truth, warning that such knowledge can destroy even an immortal soul. Hadjar's group gathers enough tokens to advance, aided by the giant heir's ability to defeat several advanced spirit knights alone. Eight hundred and eighty contestants qualify for elimination duels, and Hadjar receives a personal summons to Morgan's imperial reception.

Dora and Einen prepare Hadjar for the imperial reception, where his personal invitation distinguishes him from the other fourth-round qualifiers. The group enters a fortified imperial residence sustained by an immense magical veil. Hadjar is struck by the contrast between court wealth and deprivation elsewhere in the empire. He also learns a legend about cursed metal containing fragments of a divided soul, though its connection to the potter remains uncertain. At the gathering, Hadjar's companions separate to make political contacts. A red-haired woman then draws him aside and reveals that she is Morgan's daughter. She says conspirators intend to assassinate the emperor during the reception and asks Hadjar to help prevent the attack.

Morgan's daughter explains that a nightmare showed the emperor's death and Hadjar's soul-summoned sword. Hadjar recognizes Helmer's influence in the vision. The palace veil blocks ordinary weapons and consumes Morgan's strength while active, leaving a dangerous restoration interval if it fails. The princess believes four attackers will strike among the Guard Corps during Morgan's speech, including a nameless-level swordsman, but admits Morgan has known about her vision for months. Hadjar continues recalling Orune's Storm Mountain lessons and completes the training needed to perceive the energy pattern before lightning strikes. At the reception, the princess publicly recognizes Annis as senior heiress of the Predatory Blades clan. Hadjar quietly warns Einen, then magical darkness engulfs the hall as Morgan begins speaking.

The darkness blocks sight and World River perception while outside assassins attack Morgan's defensive formation. Hadjar orders his allies to guard the princess and uses his neural network to navigate. The nameless attacker kills a Guard Corps defender with the aid of three peak-stage lord assassins, but Hadjar realizes the guards themselves were not traitors. His primeval tigress engages the strongest foe while Hadjar kills two Laskan lord assassins. Tom helps him confront the last one, and Holy Sky School's strongest mage ends that fight. The nameless attacker then defeats the tigress and prepares to kill her. Orune arrives, freezes the battlefield within his true sword kingdom, and executes the attacker at Morgan's command. The imperial garden lies ruined, the tigress is badly injured, and Hadjar loses consciousness as the capital recognizes the assault as a step toward war with Laskan.

In a parallel Storm Mountain ordeal, Hadjar absorbs an ancient clover's pollen, flying-beast cores, and the energy of three unborn steel birds. An inner confrontation reunites him with the abandoned part of himself represented by the Quetzal, and he emerges as a Spirit Knight known as the Knight of the North Wind. After the palace battle, Dora's aunt treats Hadjar and warns that the First Darkhan fragment has grown stronger, leaving him about four years. Morgan privately reveals that he knows Hadjar as the former Mad General and prince. He wounds Hadjar for defiance but keeps him alive partly because of Orune. Hadjar concludes that Morgan permitted or arranged the crisis to expose disloyal nobles and consolidate power before war. Morgan effectively confirms this reasoning and binds Hadjar to secrecy.

Hadjar leaves the infirmary as martial law and wartime preparation reshape the capital. Remembering his breakthrough, he understands the Quetzal as an expression of his own dream and surviving self, strengthening his resolve against the First Darkhan. Orune recounts his years among brutal mercenaries and the loss of a blind dancer he loved, explaining the guilt behind his harsh philosophy. An imperial envoy later challenges Orune for taking a disciple against orders. Outside the palace, a dragon-realm emissary restrains Hadjar and questions him about the dragon heart and call inherited from his ancestor. The emissary reveals that Hadjar descends from a secondary dragon imperial branch that was exterminated after a rebellion. He admits participating in the purge and demands that Hadjar join an effort to overthrow the current dragon ruler. Hadjar refuses.

Hadjar tells the dragon emissary that he will not abandon his homeland during the approaching Laskan war. The emissary accepts the refusal temporarily and intends to return after the conflict. Hadjar reunites with Einen and Dora amid panic buying and then returns to Holy Sky School. A personal disciple warns him not to pursue a wooden token, indicating opposition within the school. Hadjar spends his accumulated glory points at the treasure tower, where an ancient golem keeper recognizes how much he has changed. He destroys the inner-circle examination golem almost immediately and receives an emerald token. Seeking movement methods capable of handling his new strength, Hadjar purchases the first volume of Orune's own technique and proceeds toward the tower's higher individualized trials.

The treasure tower strips Hadjar of cultivation advantages and places him as a mortal captain in an ancient siege. After enduring grave wounds, he recognizes that the inner sword he forged for himself cannot be taken away. That realization lets him overcome an opponent shaped like his uncle and pass the personal trial. The keeper explains that Hadjar needs power rooted in himself because no imperial strengthening method can safely supplement his altered body. For the next trial, Hadjar must create music no one has heard. He reconnects with the music that sustained him in his former life, composes an original song, and passes. His reward is a travel diary containing a route toward Path Through the Stars, the lost continuation of Path Through the Clouds that may help him overcome his divided-soul limit.

The travel diary leads toward a copy of a key to the Dragon Emperor's treasury, where Path Through the Stars was kept. Hadjar destroys the diary after preserving its clue. He joins Dora and Einen at an auction to sell the ancient fae core, despite Morgan's effort to force a cheap exchange for strategically valuable imperial resources. The giant heir renounces the Eternal Mountain Clan when his father tries to control him through a Steel Heart Pill, and Hadjar, Einen, and Tom pledge their support. When the fae heart comes up for sale, Hadjar rejects Morgan's offered sword technique. Instead, he and Einen demand imperial citizenship for neglected islands and remote kingdoms. Morgan declares them wanted criminals and orders their arrest, but Orune arrives and threatens anyone who acts against his disciple.

Elsewhere, Orune duels the Holy Sky School rector and appears defeated, but Hadjar uses the near-fatal Drawn Sword technique granted by the First Darkhan to wound the rector. Orune then reveals strength far beyond what he displayed and protects Hadjar's inherited secrets. He later tells Hadjar how Morgan once used him as a diversion in an atrocity and converted a pardon into lifelong service, warning that the emperor will exploit anyone. At the auction confrontation, Orune invokes an old law to assume Hadjar's crimes as his master. He kills himself with Morgan's sword, securing Hadjar's pardon. Morgan orders a state funeral and mourning. Supported by Einen, Dora, Annis, Tom, and the giant heir, a grieving Hadjar immediately enters the tournament's fourth round against a Dinos heir carrying the Blue Wind Sword.

The Dinos heir attacks Hadjar with the divine Blue Wind Sword, imperial armor, and powerful clan techniques. Hadjar relies on Orune's practical lessons to evade an attack believed impossible to avoid, withstand an invisible sword barrage, and continue fighting despite his grief and wounds. He resolves the relationship between his own life, his sword, and the surrounding world, manifesting barony of the sword while still only an initial-stage Spirit Knight. Hadjar kills the Dinos heir and leaves the Blue Wind Sword on the field. Orune is dead, while Einen, Dora, Annis, and the estranged giant heir survive. Tom had stood with the group after Orune's death, but his condition after the duel is not established. Hadjar's soul damage, the First Darkhan's influence, Helmer's obligations, the dragon succession claim, and the route to Path Through the Stars remain unresolved. Morgan closes the tournament moment by announcing general mobilization: Laskan troops have crossed the border, and war has begun.

characters.description: A Rain Wild girl of about sixteen, born so heavily marked that custom required she be left in the forest to die; her father took her back and raised her instead, over her mother's objections. She has black claws instead of nails, scaling across her skin, and no future her people will acknowledge, since the heavily marked are forbidden to marry or bear children. She works the canopy as a gatherer, climbs better than anyone, and has spent her life being told what she is not allowed to want.
characters.name: Thymara

characters.description: A Bingtown Trader's daughter from a family with an old name and no money, plain, freckled and bookish, who taught herself everything known about dragons and Elderlings from copied scrolls. She accepted a marriage offer from a wealthy man she barely knew, on terms that gave her an allowance and the right to pursue her study, and she means to use it.
characters.name: Alise Kincarron Finbok

characters.description: Alise's husband, a rich, handsome and fashionable Bingtown Trader who is charming in company and coldly contemptuous in private. He married for the appearance of a settled life and treats his wife's scholarship as an eccentricity to be tolerated, or used.
characters.name: Hest Finbok

characters.description: Hest's secretary, an elegant and fastidious young man who was Alise's childhood friend before he became her husband's employee. He is sent along to keep Alise company and out of trouble, resents every muddy, insect-ridden mile of the Rain Wilds, and is carrying private arrangements of his own that have nothing to do with her research.
characters.name: Sedric Meldar

characters.description: A large blue queen dragon, hatched malformed and unable to fly, who nonetheless carries herself as the aristocrat she believes she is. She has fragments of ancestral memory, contempt for humans, and an unshakeable conviction that she is owed service. She rejects the name the Rain Wilders gave her and gives her own.
characters.name: Sintara

characters.description: The captain and owner of the liveship barge Tarman, a squat, powerful river man with a rough manner, an unfashionable crew and an unusual attachment to his vessel. He knows the Rain Wild River better than anyone and is guarded about how far up it he has been.
characters.name: Leftrin

characters.description: A golden dragon, the least deformed and by far the most thoughtful of the stunted clutch. Where the others rage or sulk, he plans: it is his argument that the dragons must leave the swamp and go upriver in search of the old Elderling city, and his patience that persuades the humans to help.
characters.name: Mercor

characters.description: The liveship barge, built of wizardwood generations ago in a shape nobody builds any more, with painted eyes and thirty-odd legs he is not supposed to have. He is quieter than any other liveship and much older, and Leftrin is careful about who notices how much of him is awake.
characters.name: Tarman

characters.description: A former slave from Bingtown, tattooed across his face, who came upriver as a boy and has made a place for himself among Rain Wilders who are not sure he counts as one of them. He is steady, practical and one of the few people who has ever treated Thymara as an equal.
characters.name: Tats

characters.description: A cheerfully odd young keeper with scarlet scaling and pale eyes, who says whatever occurs to him and appears to be afraid of nothing at all. The other keepers treat him as a simpleton; his dragon is a small, greedy red queen he insists on calling Heeby.
characters.name: Rapskal

characters.description: A young keeper, small for her age and gentler than most, who attaches herself to the golden dragon Mercor and takes his dignity as her own. She grooms him obsessively and defends him to anyone who calls the dragons vermin.
characters.name: Sylve

characters.description: The oldest and most heavily marked of the keepers, a young man with a hard history who takes it for granted that he will lead.
